title.zh: 卷三百六十 列傳第一百十九 宗澤 趙鼎
title.en: Volume 360 Biographies 119: Zong Ze, Zhao Ding
title.raw: 卷三百六十 列傳第一百十九 宗澤 趙鼎 Volume 360 Biographies 119: Zong Ze, Zhao Ding

sentences.zh: 宗澤 趙鼎

translations.literal: Zong Ze; Zhao Ding
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ze and Zhao Ding

sentences.zh: 宗澤。

translations.literal: Zong Ze.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ze.

sentences.zh: 字汝霖，婺州義烏人。

translations.literal: His courtesy name was Rulin; he was a native of Yiwu in Wuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His courtesy name was Rulin, and he was from Yiwu in Wuzhou prefecture.

sentences.zh: 母劉，夢天大雷電，光燭其身，翌日而澤生。

translations.literal: His mother Liu dreamed of thunder and lightning filling heaven, its light shining upon her body; the next day Ze was born.
translations.idiomatic: His mother, née Liu, dreamed of thunder and lightning filling the sky, with light shining on her body; Ze was born the next day.

sentences.zh: 澤自幼豪爽有大志，登元祐六年進士第。

translations.literal: From youth Ze was bold and generous with great ambition; he passed the jinshi examination in the sixth year of Yuanyou.
translations.idiomatic: From childhood Zong Ze was forthright and ambitious; he passed the jinshi examination in 1091 (the sixth year of the Yuanyou reign).

sentences.zh: 廷對極陳時弊，考官惡直，置末甲。

translations.literal: In the palace examination he set forth the abuses of the age at length; the examiners disliked his bluntness and placed him last in his class.
translations.idiomatic: In his palace examination he spoke at length against the abuses of the day; the examiners resented his bluntness and ranked him last in his cohort.

sentences.zh: 調大名館陶尉。

translations.literal: He was assigned as magistrate of Guantao in Daming prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Guantao county under Daming prefecture.

sentences.zh: 呂惠卿帥鄜延，檄澤與邑令視河埽，檄至，澤適喪長子，奉檄遽行。

translations.literal: Lü Huiqing commanded Yan-Yan circuit and ordered Ze and the county magistrate to inspect river dikes; when the order arrived, Ze had just lost his eldest son, yet he took the order and hurried off.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Huiqing was military commissioner of the Yan–Yan circuit, he summoned Ze and the county magistrate to inspect river embankments. The order arrived just as Ze was mourning his eldest son, but he set out at once in obedience to it.

sentences.zh: 惠卿聞之，曰：「可謂國爾忘家者。

translations.literal: Huiqing heard of it and said: "He may be called one who forgets his family for the state.
translations.idiomatic: When Lü Huiqing heard of this, he said, "This is truly a man who puts the state before his own family."

sentences.zh: 」適朝廷大開御河，時方隆冬，役夫僵仆於道，中使督之急。

translations.literal: " At that time the court was opening the Imperial Canal on a grand scale; it was deep winter, and laborers were collapsing along the roads, while palace envoys pressed them urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Around that time the court was digging open the Imperial Canal on a grand scale. It was the depths of winter, and conscript laborers were collapsing along the roads while court envoys drove them relentlessly.

sentences.zh: 澤曰浚河細事，乃上書其帥曰：「時方凝寒，徒苦民而功未易集，少需之，至初春可不擾而辦。

translations.literal: Ze said dredging the river was a minor matter, and wrote to his commander: "It is now bitter cold; you will only torment the people while the work will not quickly succeed—wait a little; by early spring it can be done without disturbance.
translations.idiomatic: Ze considered river-dredging a minor matter and wrote to his superior: "The weather is freezing; you will only torment the people while the work will hardly be finished. Wait a little—by early spring it can be done without disturbing the people."

sentences.zh: 」卒用其言上聞，從之。

translations.literal: " In the end his words were reported upward and followed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end his advice was reported to the throne and accepted.

sentences.zh: 惠卿辟為屬，辭。

translations.literal: Huiqing invited him to serve as an aide; he declined.
translations.idiomatic: Lü Huiqing offered him a post on his staff, but he declined.

sentences.zh: 調衢州龍遊令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Longyou in Quzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Longyou county in Quzhou.

sentences.zh: 民未知學，澤為建庠序，設師儒，講論經術，風俗一變，自此擢科者相繼。

translations.literal: The people did not yet know learning; Ze built schools, appointed teachers, and lectured on the classics; customs changed entirely, and from then on those who passed examinations followed one after another.
translations.idiomatic: The people were still unacquainted with learning, so Ze established schools, appointed teachers, and lectured on the classics. Local customs were transformed, and from then on county examinees passed the civil service examinations in steady succession.

sentences.zh: 調晉州趙城令。

translations.literal: He was transferred to be magistrate of Zhaocheng in Jin prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as magistrate of Zhaocheng county in Jin prefecture.

sentences.zh: 下車，請升縣為軍，書聞，不盡如所請。

translations.literal: On taking office he petitioned to elevate the county to a military prefecture; when the memorial reached court, not all he asked was granted.
translations.idiomatic: As soon as he took office he petitioned to elevate the county to a military prefecture. When his memorial reached the court, his request was only partly granted.

sentences.zh: 澤曰：「承平時固無慮，它日有警，當知吾言矣。

translations.literal: Ze said: "In times of peace there is indeed no worry; when alarm comes another day, you will know I spoke rightly.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ze said, "In peacetime there is no cause for concern, but when danger comes you will see I was right."

sentences.zh: 」知萊州掖縣。

translations.literal: " He became magistrate of Ye county in Laizhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed magistrate of Ye county in Laizhou.

sentences.zh: 部使者得旨市牛黃，澤報曰：「方時疫癘，牛飲其毒則結為黃。

translations.literal: The circuit envoy received orders to purchase cattle bezoar; Ze replied: "An epidemic is raging; when cattle drink its poison it forms into bezoar.
translations.idiomatic: When the circuit envoy received orders to purchase cattle bezoar, Ze replied, "An epidemic is raging now; when cattle drink contaminated water it forms bezoar in their gall bladders."

sentences.zh: 今和氣橫流，牛安得黃？

translations.literal: Now harmonious qi flows everywhere—how should cattle produce bezoar?
translations.idiomatic: Now that benign weather prevails, how should cattle have bezoar?

sentences.zh: 」使者怒，欲劾邑官。

translations.literal: " The envoy was angry and wished to impeach the county officials.
translations.idiomatic: The envoy was furious and meant to impeach the county officials.

sentences.zh: 澤曰：「此澤意也。

translations.literal: Ze said: "This was Ze's idea.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ze said, "This was my doing alone."

sentences.zh: 」獨銜以聞。

translations.literal: " He alone took the blame and reported it upward.
translations.idiomatic: He alone bore responsibility and reported to his superiors.

sentences.zh: 通判登州。

translations.literal: He served as assistant prefect of Dengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He served as vice-prefect of Dengzhou.

sentences.zh: 境內官田數百頃，皆不毛之地，歲輸萬餘緡，率橫取於民，澤奏免之。

translations.literal: Within the jurisdiction were several hundred qing of government fields, all barren land, yet yearly tribute of over ten thousand strings was exacted, mostly by arbitrary levies on the people; Ze memorialized to exempt them.
translations.idiomatic: Within his jurisdiction were several hundred qing of government fields, all barren land, yet the annual levy exceeded ten thousand strings of cash, mostly extorted from the people. Ze memorialized to have the levy abolished.

sentences.zh: 時太原失守，官兩河者率托故不行。

translations.literal: At that time Taiyuan had fallen; officials for the Two He circuits mostly made excuses and would not go.
translations.idiomatic: When Taiyuan fell, officials appointed to the Two He circuits mostly pleaded excuses and refused to take up their posts.

sentences.zh: 澤曰：「食祿而避難，不可也。

translations.literal: Ze said: "To draw salary and avoid danger is not permissible.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ze said, "To draw a salary and flee from danger—that cannot be done."

sentences.zh: 」即日單騎就道，從嬴卒十餘人。

translations.literal: " That same day he went alone on horseback to his post, with a dozen-odd straggling soldiers following.
translations.idiomatic: That same day he set out alone on horseback with only a dozen or so scattered soldiers.

sentences.zh: 磁經敵騎蹂躪之餘，人民逃徙，帑廩枵然。

translations.literal: Ci prefecture had just been trampled by enemy cavalry; the people had fled, and the storehouses were empty.
translations.idiomatic: Cizhou had just been ravaged by enemy cavalry; the people had fled, and the granaries were bare.

sentences.zh: 澤至，繕城壁，浚湟池，治器械，募義勇，始為固守不移之計。

translations.literal: When Ze arrived he repaired walls, dredged moats, prepared weapons, recruited volunteers, and first formed a plan to hold firm without yielding.
translations.idiomatic: When Zong Ze arrived he repaired the walls, deepened the moats, readied weapons, recruited volunteers, and began planning a determined defense.

sentences.zh: 上言：「邢、洺、磁、趙、相五州各蓄精兵二萬人，敵攻一郡則四郡皆應，是一郡之兵常有十萬人。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "The five prefectures Xing, Ming, Ci, Zhao, and Xiang should each keep twenty thousand elite troops; if the enemy attacks one commandery the other four all respond—then one commandery's troops effectively number one hundred thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Let each of the five prefectures—Xing, Ming, Ci, Zhao, and Xiang—maintain twenty thousand elite troops. If the enemy attacks one commandery, the other four will respond, so that one commandery will always have the strength of one hundred thousand men."

sentences.zh: 」上嘉之，除河北義兵都總管。

translations.literal: " The emperor commended this and appointed him overall commander of Hebei volunteer forces.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and appointed him overall commander of Hebei volunteer forces.

sentences.zh: 金人破真定，引兵南取慶源，自李固渡渡河，恐澤兵躡其後，遣數千騎直扣磁州城。

translations.literal: The Jurchens took Zhending and led troops south toward Qingyuan; crossing at Ligu Crossing, fearing Ze's army would follow them, they sent several thousand cavalry straight at Cizhou city.
translations.idiomatic: After the Jurchens captured Zhending they marched south toward Qingyuan, crossed the Yellow River at Ligu Crossing, and, fearing Zong Ze might pursue, sent several thousand horsemen straight against Cizhou.

sentences.zh: 澤擐甲登城，令壯士以神臂弓射走之，開門縱擊，斬首數百級。

translations.literal: Ze donned armor, ascended the wall, ordered strong men to drive them off with divine arm bows, opened the gates and struck, and took several hundred heads.
translations.idiomatic: Ze donned armor and mounted the wall, had his strongest archers drive them off with crossbows, then opened the gates and sallied forth, killing several hundred of the enemy.

sentences.zh: 所獲羊馬金帛，悉以賞軍士。

translations.literal: Sheep, horses, gold, and silk captured were all given to reward the soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: He distributed all captured livestock, gold, and silk as rewards to his troops.

sentences.zh: 康王再使金，行至磁，澤迎謁曰：「肅王一去不反，今敵又詭辭以致大王，願勿行。

translations.literal: The Prince of Kang was again sent to the Jin; when he reached Ci, Ze came to meet him and said: "Prince Su went and never returned; now the enemy uses cunning words to lure Your Highness—please do not go.
translations.idiomatic: When the Prince of Kang was sent to the Jin court again and reached Cizhou, Ze met him and said, "Prince Su went north and never returned. Now the enemy is using sweet words to lure Your Highness north—please do not go."

sentences.zh: 」王遂回相州。

translations.literal: " The prince then returned to Xiangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The prince turned back to Xiangzhou.

sentences.zh: 有詔以澤為副元帥，從王起兵入援。

translations.literal: An edict made Ze deputy commander-in-chief to follow the prince in raising troops to relieve the capital.
translations.idiomatic: An edict appointed Ze deputy commander-in-chief to follow the prince in raising an army to rescue the capital.

sentences.zh: 澤言宜急會兵李固渡，斷敵歸路，眾不從，乃自將兵趨渡，道遇北兵，遣秦光弼、張德夾擊，大破之。

translations.literal: Ze said they should quickly gather troops at Ligu Crossing and cut the enemy's line of retreat; the multitude did not agree, so he himself led troops toward the crossing, met northern troops on the way, sent Qin Guangbi and Zhang De to attack from both sides, and routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: Ze urged that they quickly concentrate forces at Ligu Crossing to cut the enemy's retreat, but the others would not listen. He then led his own troops toward the crossing, met Jin forces on the road, and sent Qin Guangbi and Zhang De to strike from both flanks, winning a great victory.

sentences.zh: 金人既敗，乃留兵分屯。

translations.literal: After the Jin were defeated they left troops posted in separate camps.
translations.idiomatic: After their defeat the Jurchens left troops in scattered encampments.

sentences.zh: 澤遣壯士夜搗其軍，破三十餘砦。

translations.literal: Ze sent stalwarts to raid their camps by night and broke more than thirty stockades.
translations.idiomatic: Ze sent picked men to raid their camps by night and destroyed more than thirty of them.

sentences.zh: 時康王開大元帥府，檄兵會大名。

translations.literal: At that time the Prince of Kang opened the Grand Marshal's headquarters and ordered troops to assemble at Daming.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Kang established the Grand Marshal's headquarters and ordered troops to assemble at Daming.

sentences.zh: 澤履冰渡河見王，謂京城受圍日久，入援不可緩。

translations.literal: Ze crossed the river on ice to see the prince and said the capital had been besieged long—relief could not be delayed.
translations.idiomatic: Ze crossed the frozen river to see the prince and argued that the capital had been under siege for a long time and relief could not wait.

sentences.zh: 會簽書樞密院事曹輔齎蠟封欽宗手詔，至自京師，言和議可成。

translations.literal: Just then Privy Council signatory Cao Fu arrived from the capital bearing Emperor Qinzong's sealed handwritten edict, saying peace talks could succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Just then Privy Council signatory Cao Fu arrived from the capital with a sealed handwritten edict from Emperor Qinzong, stating that peace could be negotiated.

sentences.zh: 澤曰：「金人狡譎，是欲款我師爾。

translations.literal: Ze said: "The Jin are crafty—this is only to parley with our army.
translations.idiomatic: Ze said, "The Jurchens are cunning—they only want to stall our army."

sentences.zh: 君父之望入援，何啻饑渴，宜急引軍直趨澶淵，次第進壘，以解京城之圍。

translations.literal: The sovereign and father's hope for relief is no less than thirst and hunger—you should urgently lead the army straight to Chanzhou, advancing camps step by step to lift the siege of the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Your father the emperor longs for relief as a man longs for food and drink in famine. Lead the army straight to Chanzhou at once, advance camp by camp, and lift the siege of the capital.

sentences.zh: 萬一敵有異謀，則吾兵已在城下。

translations.literal: If by chance the enemy have other designs, our troops will already be below the walls.
translations.idiomatic: If the enemy should plot something else, our army will already be at the city walls.

sentences.zh: 」汪伯彥等難之，勸王遣澤先行，自是澤不得預府中謀議矣。

translations.literal: " Wang Boyan and others objected, urging the prince to send Ze ahead first—from then on Ze was shut out of headquarters deliberations.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Boyan and others objected and urged the prince to send Ze ahead first; from then on Ze was excluded from deliberations at headquarters.

sentences.zh: 二年正月，澤至開德，十三戰皆捷，以書勸王檄諸道兵會京城。

translations.literal: In the first month of the second year Ze reached Kaide; thirteen battles were all victories, and he wrote urging the prince to dispatch orders summoning troops from all circuits to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of year two of the Jingkang era, Ze reached Kaide, won thirteen battles in succession, and wrote urging the prince to issue orders summoning troops from all circuits to the capital.

sentences.zh: 又移書北道總管趙野、河東北路宣撫範訥、知興仁府曾楙合兵入援。

translations.literal: He also sent letters to Northern Route commander Zhao Ye, Hedong-Hebei North Route commissioner Fan Ne, and Xingren prefecture intendant Zeng Mao to join forces in relief.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote to Northern Route commander Zhao Ye, Hedong–Hebei North commissioner Fan Ne, and Xingren prefecture intendant Zeng Mao urging them to combine forces for relief.

sentences.zh: 三人皆以澤為狂，不答。

translations.literal: All three regarded Ze as mad and did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: All three regarded Ze as reckless and ignored him.

sentences.zh: 澤以孤軍進，都統陳淬言敵方熾，未可輕舉。

translations.literal: Ze advanced with an isolated army; commander-in-chief Chen Cui said the enemy's strength was blazing and one should not act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: Ze pressed forward with a lone army. Commander Chen Cui said the enemy was too strong and they should not act rashly.

sentences.zh: 澤怒，欲斬之，諸將乞貸淬，使得效死。

translations.literal: Ze was angry and wished to execute him; the generals begged to spare Cui and let him die fighting.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was furious and wanted to execute him, but the generals pleaded for Chen Cui's life so he could fight to the death.

sentences.zh: 澤命淬進兵，遇金人，敗之。

translations.literal: Ze ordered Cui to advance; they met Jin troops and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Ze ordered Chen Cui to advance; when they met Jin forces he routed them.

sentences.zh: 金人攻開德，澤遣孔彥威與戰，又敗之。

translations.literal: The Jin attacked Kaide; Ze sent Kong Yanwei to fight and again defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked Kaide, Ze sent Kong Yanwei to meet them and won again.

sentences.zh: 澤度金人必犯濮，先遣三千騎往援，金人果至，敗之。

translations.literal: Ze judged the Jin must attack Pu prefecture, first sent three thousand cavalry to aid; the Jin indeed came and were defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Ze predicted the Jin would strike Pu prefecture and sent three thousand cavalry ahead; when they arrived he defeated them.

sentences.zh: 金人復向開德，權邦彥、孔彥威合兵夾擊，又大敗之。

translations.literal: The Jin again turned toward Kaide; Quan Bangyan and Kong Yanwei combined forces in a pincer attack and again routed them utterly.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin turned on Kaide again, Quan Bangyan and Kong Yanwei combined forces and struck them from both sides, winning another great victory.

sentences.zh: 澤兵進至衛南，度將孤兵寡，不深入不能成功。

translations.literal: Ze's army advanced to Weinan; he judged that with few isolated troops, without pressing deep they could not succeed.
translations.idiomatic: Ze's army advanced to Weinan. He judged that with so few troops, they could not succeed without pushing deep into enemy territory.

sentences.zh: 先驅云前有敵營，澤揮眾直前與戰，敗之。

translations.literal: The vanguard reported an enemy camp ahead; Ze waved the host straight forward to fight and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the vanguard reported an enemy camp ahead, Ze led his men straight forward, fought, and won.

sentences.zh: 轉戰而東，敵益生兵至，王孝忠戰死，前後皆敵壘。

translations.literal: Fighting eastward, more and more enemy reinforcements arrived; Wang Xiaozhong died in battle, and enemy stockades lay before and behind.
translations.idiomatic: As they fought eastward more enemy reinforcements arrived; Wang Xiaozhong was killed in battle, and enemy camps lay ahead and behind them.

sentences.zh: 澤下令曰：「今日進退等死，不可不從死中求生。

translations.literal: Ze gave the order: "Today advance and retreat are alike death—we must seek life from within death.
translations.idiomatic: Ze ordered, "Today advance and retreat mean the same death—we must win life out of death."

sentences.zh: 」士卒知必死，無不一當百，斬首數千級。

translations.literal: " The soldiers knew they must die; each fought as a hundred, and several thousand heads were taken.
translations.idiomatic: Knowing they faced certain death, every man fought as if he were worth a hundred; they took several thousand enemy heads.

sentences.zh: 金人大敗，退卻數十餘里。

translations.literal: The Jin were utterly defeated and retreated more than ten li.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin were routed and fell back more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 澤計敵眾十倍於我，今一戰而卻，勢必復來，使悉其鐵騎夜襲吾軍，則危矣。

translations.literal: Ze calculated the enemy were ten times our number; now after one battle they retreated—they were sure to return; if they sent all their armored cavalry to raid us by night, it would be perilous.
translations.idiomatic: Ze reckoned the enemy outnumbered his force ten to one. Having been beaten back once, they were sure to return, and if they sent all their armored cavalry to raid his camp by night, his position would be desperate.

sentences.zh: 乃暮徙其軍。

translations.literal: At dusk he moved his army.
translations.idiomatic: At dusk he moved his army to another position.

sentences.zh: 金人夜至，得空營，大驚，自是憚澤，不敢復出兵。

translations.literal: The Jin came by night and found empty camps; greatly alarmed, from then on they feared Ze and dared not send troops again.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin came by night and found an empty camp. Greatly alarmed, from then on they feared Ze and dared not venture out again.

sentences.zh: 澤出其不意，遣兵過大河襲擊，敗之。

translations.literal: Ze took them unawares, sent troops across the great river to raid, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: Taking them by surprise, he sent troops across the Yellow River to raid them and won again.

sentences.zh: 王承制以澤為徽猷閣待制。

translations.literal: The prince, acting on his own authority, appointed Ze Attendant Gentleman in the Huiyao Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: The prince, acting on emergency authority, appointed Ze Attendant Gentleman in the Huiyao Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 時金人逼二帝北行，澤聞，即提軍趨滑，走黎陽，至大名，欲徑渡河，據金人歸路邀還二帝，而勤王之兵卒無一至者。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin were forcing the two emperors north; when Ze heard, he immediately led his army toward Hua, went through Liyang to Daming, wished to cross directly, hold the Jin's line of retreat and rescue the two emperors—but not a single loyalist relief army came.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin were escorting the two emperors north, Ze heard the news and immediately marched toward Hua, passed through Liyang to Daming, and intended to cross the river straightaway, block the Jin line of retreat, and recover the two emperors—but not a single loyalist relief army ever arrived.

sentences.zh: 又聞張邦昌僭位，欲先行誅討。

translations.literal: He also heard Zhang Bangchang had usurped the throne and wished to punish him first.
translations.idiomatic: Learning that Zhang Bangchang had usurped the throne, he wanted to strike him down first.

sentences.zh: 會得大元帥府書，約移師近都，按甲觀變。

translations.literal: Then he received a letter from the Grand Marshal's headquarters, arranging to move the army near the capital and hold arms while watching events.
translations.idiomatic: Then he received word from the Grand Marshal's headquarters arranging for him to move his army near the capital and hold his troops in readiness while observing events.

sentences.zh: 澤覆書于王曰：「人臣豈有服赭袍、張紅蓋、御正殿者乎？

translations.literal: Ze replied to the prince: "Can a subject wear the ochre robe, raise the red canopy, and preside in the main hall?
translations.idiomatic: Ze wrote back to the prince: "What subject may wear the imperial ochre robe, raise the red imperial canopy, and sit in the main hall of the palace?"

sentences.zh: 自古奸臣皆外為恭順而中藏禍心，未有竊據寶位、改元肆赦、惡狀昭著若邦昌者。

translations.literal: Since ancient times treacherous ministers outwardly showed deference while hiding evil hearts within—never has one seized the imperial seat, changed the era name, issued a general amnesty, and shown crimes as plainly as Bangchang.
translations.idiomatic: Treacherous ministers have always worn a mask of obedience while hiding evil designs within, but never before has anyone seized the throne, changed the reign title, proclaimed a general amnesty, and displayed his crimes as openly as Zhang Bangchang.

sentences.zh: 今二聖、諸王悉渡河而北，惟大王在濟，天意可知，宜亟行天討，興復社稷。

translations.literal: Now the two sage emperors and all princes have crossed the river north; only Your Highness remains at Ji—Heaven's intent is clear; you should swiftly carry out Heaven's punishment and restore the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: Now both emperors and all the princes have been taken north across the river; only Your Highness remains at Ji. Heaven's intent is clear—you should swiftly punish this usurper and restore the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 」且言：「邦昌偽赦，或啟奸雄之意，望遣使分諭諸路，以定民心。

translations.literal: " He also said: "Bangchang's false amnesty may awaken the ambition of other traitors—I hope you will send envoys to explain separately to each circuit and settle popular hearts.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote that Zhang Bangchang's sham amnesty might awaken the ambitions of other traitors, and urged the prince to send envoys to every circuit to steady the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 」又上書言：「今天下所屬望者在於大王，大王行之得其道，則有心慰天下之心。

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "Today all under Heaven look to Your Highness; if Your Highness acts according to the Way, you will comfort the hearts of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In another memorial he wrote that all under Heaven now looked to the prince, and that if the prince followed the right path he would comfort the hearts of the empire.

sentences.zh: 所謂道者，近剛正而遠柔邪，納諫諍而拒諛佞，尚恭儉而抑驕侈，體憂勤而忘逸樂，進公實而退私偽。

translations.literal: What is called the Way is: draw near to the upright and keep away the soft and evil; accept remonstrance and reject flattery; esteem respect and frugality and restrain pride and extravagance; embody care and diligence and forget ease and pleasure; advance what is public and real and dismiss what is private and false.
translations.idiomatic: The Way, he said, meant drawing close to the upright and keeping the crafty at a distance, welcoming frank counsel and rejecting flatterers, practicing restraint and checking extravagance, sharing the people's burdens and shunning pleasure, and promoting what served the public good while rejecting selfish fraud.

sentences.zh: 」因累表勸進。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he submitted repeated memorials urging the prince to ascend.
translations.idiomatic: He repeatedly memorialized urging the prince to take the throne.

sentences.zh: 王即帝位于南京，澤入見，涕泗交頤，陳興復大計。

translations.literal: The prince took the throne at Nanjing; Ze entered audience, tears streaming down his face, and set forth the great plan of restoration.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince took the throne at Nanjing, Ze had an audience with him. Tears streaming down his face, he laid out the great plan for restoring the dynasty.

sentences.zh: 時與李綱同入對，相見論國事，慷慨流涕，綱奇之。

translations.literal: At that time he entered audience together with Li Gang; meeting they discussed state affairs, speaking fervently with flowing tears; Gang marveled at him.
translations.idiomatic: He entered audience together with Li Gang; when they met they discussed state affairs with such passion that both wept, and Li Gang marveled at him.

sentences.zh: 上欲留澤，潛善等沮之。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to keep Ze; Qian Shan and others obstructed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to keep Ze at court, but Huang Qianshan and his faction blocked it.

sentences.zh: 除龍圖閣學士、知襄陽府。

translations.literal: He was appointed Dragon Diagram Hall academician and prefect of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed academician of the Dragon Diagram Hall and prefect of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 時金人有割地之議，澤上疏曰：「天下者，太祖、太宗之天下，陛下當兢兢業業，思傳之萬世，奈何遽議割河之東、西，又議割陝之蒲、解乎。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin were discussing ceding territory; Ze memorialized: "All under Heaven is the all-under-Heaven of Taizu and Taizong—Your Majesty should be cautious and reverent, thinking to pass it down ten thousand generations—how can you hastily discuss ceding east and west of the River, and also discuss ceding Pu and Jie in Shaan?
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin were pressing for territorial concessions, Ze memorialized: "All under Heaven belonged to Taizu and Taizong. Your Majesty should be ever vigilant, thinking to pass the realm down through ten thousand generations—how can you hastily discuss ceding the lands east and west of the Yellow River, and even Pu and Jie in Shaanxi?"

sentences.zh: 自金人再至，朝廷未嘗命一將、出一師，但聞奸邪之臣，朝進一言以告和，暮入一說以乞盟，終致二聖北遷，宗社蒙恥。

translations.literal: Since the Jin came again, the court never ordered a single general or sent out a single army—only heard of wicked ministers, one proposal for peace in the morning, one plea for alliance at evening, ending with the two sage emperors moved north and the altars of state shamed.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Jin invaded again the court has never appointed a single general or dispatched a single army—we have only heard wicked ministers, one urging peace in the morning and another pleading for alliance at night—until both emperors were taken north and the dynasty was disgraced.

sentences.zh: 臣意陛下赫然震怒，大明黜陟，以再造王室。

translations.literal: This subject's thought is that Your Majesty should be suddenly aroused in wrath, clearly reward and punish, to recreate the royal house.
translations.idiomatic: I believe Your Majesty should be stirred to righteous anger, clearly reward the loyal and punish the guilty, and thus rebuild the royal house.

sentences.zh: 今即位四十日矣，未聞有大號令，但見刑部指揮云'不得謄播赦文於河之東、西，陝之蒲、解'者，是褫天下忠義之氣，而自絕其民也。

translations.literal: Now forty days since enthronement, no great proclamation has been heard—only seen a Ministry of Justice directive saying 'do not copy and proclaim amnesty documents east and west of the River, at Pu and Jie in Shaan'—this strips all loyalists under Heaven of their spirit and cuts yourself off from your people.
translations.idiomatic: Forty days have passed since Your Majesty took the throne, yet no great proclamation has been issued—only a Ministry of Justice order forbidding amnesty notices to be circulated east and west of the Yellow River or in Pu and Jie. This crushes the loyal spirit of the empire and cuts Your Majesty off from your own people.

sentences.zh: 臣雖駑怯，當躬冒矢石為諸將先，得捐軀報國恩足矣。

translations.literal: Though this subject is weak and timid, I should personally brave arrows and stones ahead of the generals; to give my body repaying the state's grace is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Weak and timid as I am, I am ready to face arrows and stones ahead of all your generals; it would be enough to give my life repaying the state's kindness.

sentences.zh: 」上覽其言壯之。

translations.literal: The emperor read his words and found them bold.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor read his memorial and was impressed by its boldness.

sentences.zh: 改知青州，時年六十九矣。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Qingzhou; he was then sixty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to serve as prefect of Qingzhou; he was sixty-nine years old.

sentences.zh: 開封尹闕，李綱言綏復舊都，非澤不可。

translations.literal: The Kaifeng intendant post was vacant; Li Gang said to soothe and restore the old capital, none but Ze would do.
translations.idiomatic: When the Kaifeng intendant post fell vacant, Li Gang said that pacifying and restoring the old capital required no one but Zong Ze.

sentences.zh: 尋徙知開封府。

translations.literal: Soon he was transferred to intendant of Kaifeng prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was transferred to serve as prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 時敵騎留屯河上，金鼓之聲，日夕相聞，而京城樓櫓盡廢，兵民雜居，盜賊縱橫，人情忷忷。

translations.literal: At that time enemy cavalry lingered encamped on the river; sounds of drums and bells were heard morning and evening, yet the capital's towers were all ruined, soldiers and civilians mixed in residence, bandits ran rampant, and popular sentiment was alarmed.
translations.idiomatic: Enemy cavalry still camped on the north bank of the river, and the clash of arms could be heard day and night. The capital's watchtowers lay in ruins, soldiers and civilians were crowded together, bandits ran rampant, and the people were in a panic.

sentences.zh: 澤威望素著，既至，首捕誅舍賊者數人。

translations.literal: Ze's prestige had always been renowned; once he arrived, he first captured and executed several dwelling-bandits.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ze's prestige was already well established. As soon as he arrived he arrested and executed several housebreakers.

sentences.zh: 下令曰：「為盜者，贓無輕重，並從軍法。

translations.literal: He issued an order: "Those who steal—the weight of loot does not matter; all are subject to military law.
translations.idiomatic: He issued an order: "Anyone who steals, regardless of the value of the loot, will be dealt with under military law."

sentences.zh: 」由是盜賊屏息，民賴以安。

translations.literal: " Thereupon bandits held their breath and the people relied on this for peace.
translations.idiomatic: After that bandits dared not stir, and the people were secure.

sentences.zh: 王善者，河東巨寇也。

translations.literal: Wang Shan was a great bandit of Hedong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shan was a great bandit chieftain of Hedong.

sentences.zh: 擁眾七十萬、車萬乘，欲據京城。

translations.literal: He held a host of seven hundred thousand and ten thousand chariots, and wished to seize the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He commanded a force said to number seven hundred thousand with ten thousand wagons, and intended to seize the capital.

sentences.zh: 澤單騎馳至善營，泣謂之曰：「朝廷當危難之時，使有如公一二輩，豈復有敵患乎。

translations.literal: Ze rode alone at full speed to Shan's camp, weeping and saying: "When the court faces crisis and danger, if there were one or two men like you, would there still be enemy peril?
translations.idiomatic: Ze rode alone at full speed to Wang Shan's camp, wept, and said to him, "At a time when the dynasty faces mortal danger, if the court had even one or two men like you, would we still fear any enemy?"

sentences.zh: 今日乃汝立功之秋，不可失也。

translations.literal: Today is the season for you to achieve merit—do not let it pass.
translations.idiomatic: Today is the season for you to win glory—do not let it slip away.

sentences.zh: 」善感泣曰：「敢不效力。

translations.literal: " Shan was moved to tears and said: "How dare I not exert my strength.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shan wept and said, "How could I refuse to serve?"

sentences.zh: 」遂解甲降。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he doffed his armor and surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he laid down his arms and surrendered.

sentences.zh: 時楊進號沒角牛，兵三十萬，王再興、李貴、王大郎等各擁眾數萬，往來京西、淮南、河南、北，侵掠為患。

translations.literal: At that time Yang Jin, styled Missing Horn Ox, had three hundred thousand troops; Wang Zaixing, Li Gui, Wang Dalang, and others each held hosts of tens of thousands, ranging through western Jing, Huainan, Henan north and south, plundering and causing harm.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Yang Jin, known as "Missing Horn Ox," commanded three hundred thousand men, while Wang Zaixing, Li Gui, Wang Dalang, and others each led forces of tens of thousands, raiding back and forth across western Jing, Huainan, and Henan and bringing misery wherever they went.

sentences.zh: 澤遣人諭以禍福，悉招降之。

translations.literal: Ze sent men to explain fortune and disaster, and all were persuaded to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Ze sent envoys to explain the consequences and won them all over to surrender.

sentences.zh: 上疏請上還京。

translations.literal: He memorialized asking the emperor to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized urging the emperor to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 俄有詔：荊、襄、江、淮悉備巡幸。

translations.literal: Soon an edict came: Jing, Xiang, Jiang, and Huai were all to prepare for imperial progress.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict ordered the Jing, Xiang, Yangtze, and Huai regions to prepare for an imperial tour.

sentences.zh: 澤上疏言：「開封物價市肆，漸同平時。

translations.literal: Ze memorialized saying: "In Kaifeng, prices and markets are gradually like normal times.
translations.idiomatic: Ze memorialized: "In Kaifeng, market prices and shops are gradually returning to normal."

sentences.zh: 將士、農民、商旅、士大夫之懷忠義者，莫不願陛下亟歸京師，以慰人心。

translations.literal: Soldiers, farmers, merchants, and scholars who cherish loyalty and righteousness all wish Your Majesty would swiftly return to the capital to comfort people's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers, farmers, merchants, travelers, and loyal scholars all long for Your Majesty to return to the capital at once and steady the people's hearts.

sentences.zh: 其唱為異議者，非為陛下忠謀，不過如張邦昌輩，陰與金人為地爾。

translations.literal: Those who raise dissenting voices do not plot loyally for Your Majesty—they are merely like Zhang Bangchang's sort, secretly making ground for the Jin.
translations.idiomatic: Those who urge otherwise are not serving Your Majesty's true interest—they are merely men of Zhang Bangchang's sort, secretly paving the way for the Jin."

sentences.zh: 」除延康殿學士、京城留守、兼開封尹。

translations.literal: " He was appointed academician of the Yankang Hall, capital garrison commander, and also Kaifeng intendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed academician of the Yankang Hall, defender of the capital, and concurrent prefect of Kaifeng.

sentences.zh: 時金遣人以使偽楚為名，至開封府，澤曰：「此名為使，而實覘我也。

translations.literal: At that time the Jin sent men under the name of envoys to the false Chu state; arriving at Kaifeng prefecture, Ze said: "Though called envoys, in truth they spy on us.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin sent envoys under the pretense of diplomatic contact with the puppet Chu regime, Ze said at Kaifeng, "They call themselves envoys, but in truth they are spies."

sentences.zh: 」拘其人，乞斬之。

translations.literal: " He detained them and asked to execute them.
translations.idiomatic: He detained them and petitioned to have them executed.

sentences.zh: 有詔所拘金使延置別館，澤曰：「國家承平二百年，不識兵革，以敵國誕謾為可憑信，恬不置疑。

translations.literal: An edict ordered the detained Jin envoys lodged in a separate hostel; Ze said: "The state has enjoyed peace two hundred years and knows not arms; taking enemy grand lies as trustworthy, one placidly suspects nothing.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict ordered the detained Jin envoys lodged in a separate hostel, Ze said, "Our dynasty has known peace for two hundred years and scarcely remembers war. To treat the enemy's brazen lies as trustworthy, and never question them—

sentences.zh: 不惟不嚴攻討之計，其有實欲賈勇思敵所愾之人，士大夫不以為狂，則以為妄，致有前日之禍。

translations.literal: Not only are there no strict plans of attack, but those who truly wish to sell their courage and think of what the enemy hate—scholars-officials call them mad or deem them reckless, bringing the calamity of other days.
translations.idiomatic: not only have we failed to plan a serious counterattack, but when men truly burn to fight the enemy, officials call them mad or reckless. That is how we brought yesterday's disaster upon ourselves."

sentences.zh: 張邦昌、耿南仲輩所為，陛下所親見也。

translations.literal: What Zhang Bangchang, Geng Nanzhong's sort, did—Your Majesty saw with your own eyes.
translations.idiomatic: What Zhang Bangchang, Geng Nanzhong, and men like them did—Your Majesty saw with your own eyes."

sentences.zh: 今金人假使偽楚，來覘虛實，臣愚乞斬之，以破其奸。

translations.literal: Now the Jin falsely send envoys to false Chu to spy on our condition; this subject humbly asks to execute them to break their treachery.
translations.idiomatic: Now the Jin send these spies under the false Chu pretense. I beg Your Majesty to execute them and break their intrigue."

sentences.zh: 而陛下惑于人言，令遷置別館，優加待遇，臣愚不敢奉詔，以彰國弱。

translations.literal: Yet Your Majesty is misled by men's words, ordering them moved to a separate hostel with generous treatment—I humbly dare not obey the edict, lest it display national weakness.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Your Majesty, swayed by others' words, has them moved to a hostel and treated generously. I dare not obey such an edict, for it would proclaim our weakness to the world."

sentences.zh: 」上乃親劄諭澤，竟縱遣之。

translations.literal: " The emperor then personally wrote to instruct Ze, but in the end let them go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wrote a personal letter instructing Ze, but in the end the envoys were released.

sentences.zh: 言者附潛善意，皆以澤拘留金使為非。

translations.literal: Critics siding with Qian Shan's intent all deemed Ze's detention of the Jin envoys wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Critics aligned with Huang Qianshan all condemned Ze for detaining the Jin envoys.

sentences.zh: 尚書左丞許景衡抗疏力辨，且謂：「澤之為尹，威名政績，卓然過人，今之縉紳，未見其比。

translations.literal: Left Vice Director Xu Jingheng submitted a counter-memorial arguing forcefully, also saying: "In Ze's conduct as intendant, prestige, governance, and achievement surpass others—among present gentry and officials, none equal him.
translations.idiomatic: Left Vice Director Xu Jingheng submitted a strong counter-memorial arguing that "As intendant, Zong Ze's reputation and achievements surpass all others among officials today.

sentences.zh: 乞厚加任使，以成禦敵治民之功。」

translations.literal: I beg he be richly employed to accomplish the merit of repelling enemies and governing the people."
translations.idiomatic: I beg that he be given greater authority to fulfill his work of repelling the enemy and governing the people."

sentences.zh: 真定、懷、衛間，敵兵甚盛，方密修戰具為入攻之計，而將相恬不為慮，不修武備，澤以為憂。

translations.literal: Between Zhending, Huai, and Wei, enemy troops were very strong, secretly preparing weapons for an invasion plan, yet ministers and generals were placidly unconcerned and did not ready arms—Ze was worried.
translations.idiomatic: Between Zhending, Huai, and Wei the enemy was very strong and was secretly preparing for an invasion, yet ministers and generals remained unconcerned and neglected military readiness. Ze was deeply worried.

sentences.zh: 乃渡河約諸將共議事宜，以圖收復，而於京城四壁，各置使以領招集之兵。

translations.literal: He then crossed the river to summon generals to discuss affairs jointly, planning recovery, and on the capital's four walls placed commissioners each to lead recruited troops.
translations.idiomatic: He crossed the river to summon the generals for joint planning toward recovery, and on each of the capital's four walls appointed commissioners to lead the recruited troops.

sentences.zh: 又據形勢立堅壁二十四所於城外，沿河鱗次為連珠砦，連結河東、河北山水砦忠義民兵，於是陝西、京東西諸路人馬咸願聽澤節制。

translations.literal: He also according to terrain established twenty-four strong forts outside the walls, along the river set up linked stockades like beads on a string, linked Hedong and Hebei mountain-and-water stockade loyal militia—thereupon forces from Shaanxi, eastern and western Jing all wished to obey Ze's command.
translations.idiomatic: He also established twenty-four strong forts outside the walls according to the terrain, set up a chain of stockades along the river, and linked the loyal militia of the mountain stockades of Hedong and Hebei. Thereupon troops from Shaanxi and eastern and western Jing all wished to serve under his command.

sentences.zh: 有詔如淮甸。

translations.literal: An edict ordered him to go to the Huai region.
translations.idiomatic: An edict ordered him to proceed to the Huai region.

sentences.zh: 澤上表諫，不報。

translations.literal: Ze submitted a memorial remonstrating; no reply came.
translations.idiomatic: Ze memorialized in protest, but received no reply.

sentences.zh: 秉義郎岳飛犯法將刑，澤一見奇之，曰：「此將材也。

translations.literal: Palace Gentleman Yue Fei had violated the law and was to be punished; at first sight Ze marveled at him and said: "This is general's timber.
translations.idiomatic: When Palace Gentleman Yue Fei faced execution for a military offense, Ze took one look at him and said, "This man has the makings of a great general."

sentences.zh: 」會金人攻汜水，澤以五百騎授飛，使立功贖罪。

translations.literal: " Just then the Jin attacked Sishui; Ze gave Fei five hundred cavalry to win merit and redeem his crime.
translations.idiomatic: Just then the Jin attacked Sishui. Ze gave Yue Fei five hundred cavalry and told him to redeem himself by winning merit in battle.

sentences.zh: 飛大敗金人而還，遂升飛為統制，飛由是知名。

translations.literal: Fei utterly defeated the Jin and returned; Ze then promoted Fei to commander—Fei became famous from this.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei routed the Jin and returned. Ze promoted him to commander, and from that day Yue Fei became famous.

sentences.zh: 澤視師河北還，上疏言：「陛下尚留南都，道路籍籍，咸以為陛下舍宗廟朝廷，使社稷無依，生靈失所仰戴。

translations.literal: Ze inspected troops in Hebei and returned, memorializing: "Your Majesty still remains at the Southern Capital; along the roads there is widespread talk that Your Majesty has abandoned the ancestral temples and court, leaving the altars of state without support and the people without whom to look up to.
translations.idiomatic: After inspecting troops in Hebei, Ze memorialized: "Your Majesty still remains at the Southern Capital. Along every road people whisper that you have abandoned the ancestral temples and court, leaving the altars of state without support and the people without a sovereign to look to.

sentences.zh: 陛下宜亟回汴京，以慰元元之心。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should swiftly return to Bianjing to comfort the hearts of the masses.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should return to Bianjing at once to comfort the hearts of the people."

sentences.zh: 」不報。

translations.literal: " No reply came.
translations.idiomatic: He received no reply.

sentences.zh: 復抗疏言：「國家結好金人，欲以息民，卒之劫掠侵欺，靡所不至，是守和議果不足以息民也。

translations.literal: He again submitted a counter-memorial saying: "The state made friendship with the Jin wishing to give the people rest—in the end plunder and aggression reached everywhere; thus keeping the peace treaty truly could not give the people rest.
translations.idiomatic: He submitted another strong memorial: "The state sought friendship with the Jin to give the people peace, yet in the end plunder and aggression knew no bounds. Keeping the peace treaty truly could not give the people peace.

sentences.zh: 當時固有阿意順旨以叨富貴者，亦有不相詭隨以獲罪戾者。

translations.literal: At that time there were certainly those who flattered intent and followed edicts to grasp wealth and rank, and also those who would not go along with deception and incurred punishment.
translations.idiomatic: At that time there were certainly those who flattered the court to win wealth and rank, and also those who refused to go along with deception and were punished.

sentences.zh: 陛下觀之，昔富貴者為是乎？

translations.literal: Your Majesty observes—which were right, those who were wealthy and noble before?
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty may judge—which were right, those who grew wealthy and noble then?

sentences.zh: 獲罪戾者為是乎？

translations.literal: Or those who incurred punishment?
translations.idiomatic: Or those who were punished?

sentences.zh: 今之言遷幸者，猶前之言和議為可行者也；

translations.literal: Today's advocates of moving the court are like yesterday's saying the peace treaty was feasible;
translations.idiomatic: Today's advocates of moving the court are like yesterday's advocates of peace who said it was feasible;

sentences.zh: 今之言不可遷者，猶前日之言和議不可行者也。

translations.literal: today's advocates of not moving are like the other day's saying the peace treaty could not be carried out.
translations.idiomatic: and today's advocates of not moving are like yesterday's opponents who said peace could not work.

sentences.zh: 惟陛下熟思而審用之。

translations.literal: Only Your Majesty should ponder deeply and employ it carefully.
translations.idiomatic: I beg Your Majesty to ponder this deeply and choose wisely.

sentences.zh: 且京師二百年積累之基業，陛下奈何輕棄以遺敵國乎。」

translations.literal: Moreover, the capital is two hundred years of accumulated foundation—how can Your Majesty lightly abandon it and leave it to the enemy state?"
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the capital is two centuries of accumulated foundation—how can Your Majesty lightly abandon it to the enemy?"

sentences.zh: 詔遣官迎奉六宮往金陵，澤上疏曰：「京師，天下腹心也。

translations.literal: An edict sent officials to escort the six palaces to Jinling; Ze memorialized: "The capital is the belly and heart of all under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: When an edict sent officials to escort the imperial household to Jinling, Ze memorialized: "The capital is the heart of the empire.

sentences.zh: 兩河雖未敉寧，特一手臂之不信爾。

translations.literal: Though the Two He are not yet pacified, it is only that one arm is not yet trusted.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Two He are not yet pacified, that is only because one arm of the realm is not yet secure.

sentences.zh: 今遽欲去之，非惟一臂之弗瘳，且並與腹心而棄之矣。

translations.literal: Now you hastily wish to leave it—not only will one arm not be healed, but you will abandon the belly and heart together.
translations.idiomatic: To leave it now will not heal that arm—it will abandon the heart along with it.

sentences.zh: 昔景德間，契丹寇澶淵，王欽若江南人，即勸幸金陵，陳堯叟蜀人，即勸幸成都，惟寇准毅然請親征，卒用成功。

translations.literal: In the Jingde era, the Khitan raided Chanzhou; Wang Qinruo, a man of Jiangnan, at once urged progress to Jinling; Chen Yaosou, a man of Shu, at once urged progress to Chengdu—only Kou Zhun resolutely asked for a personal campaign, and in the end success was achieved.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jingde era, when the Khitan attacked Chanzhou, Wang Qinruo of Jiangnan urged retreat to Jinling and Chen Yaosou of Shu urged retreat to Chengdu—only Kou Zhun resolutely demanded that the emperor take the field in person, and victory followed.

sentences.zh: 臣何敢望寇准，然不敢不以章聖望陛下。

translations.literal: How dare this subject hope to equal Kou Zhun—yet I dare not fail to hold up Emperor Zhangsheng as the model for Your Majesty.
translations.idiomatic: I dare not compare myself to Kou Zhun, yet I dare not fail to hold up Emperor Zhenzong as the model for Your Majesty."

sentences.zh: 」又條上五事，其一言黃潛善、汪伯彥贊南幸之非。

translations.literal: " He also listed five items, the first saying Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan praised the error of southern progress.
translations.idiomatic: He also listed five points, the first condemning Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan for supporting the move south.

sentences.zh: 澤前後建議，經從三省、樞密院，輒為潛善等所抑，每見澤奏疏，皆笑以為狂。

translations.literal: Ze's proposals before and after, passing through the Three Departments and Privy Council, were always suppressed by Qian Shan and others; whenever they saw Ze's memorials they laughed and called them mad.
translations.idiomatic: Ze's proposals, submitted through the Three Departments and Privy Council, were always blocked by Huang Qianshan and his faction, who laughed at his memorials and called them mad.

sentences.zh: 金將兀術渡河，謀攻汴京。

translations.literal: Jin general Wuzhu crossed the river, planning to attack Bianjing.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Wuzhu crossed the river, planning to attack Bianjing.

sentences.zh: 諸將請先斷河梁，嚴兵自固，澤笑曰：「去冬，金騎直來，正坐斷河梁耳。

translations.literal: The generals asked first to cut the river bridge and strengthen troops to hold firm; Ze laughed and said: "Last winter, Jin cavalry came straight here—precisely because the river bridge was cut.
translations.idiomatic: The generals urged cutting the river bridge and strengthening defenses. Ze laughed and said, "Last winter the Jin cavalry came straight here precisely because we had cut the bridge.

sentences.zh: 」乃命部將劉衍趨滑、劉達趨鄭，以分敵勢，戒諸將極力保護河梁，以俟大兵之集。

translations.literal: " He then ordered subordinates Liu Yan toward Hua and Liu Da toward Zheng to divide enemy strength, admonishing the generals to protect the river bridge with all effort while awaiting the gathering of the great army.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered his subordinates Liu Yan toward Hua and Liu Da toward Zheng to divide the enemy's strength, and warned the generals to defend the river crossing at all costs while awaiting the main army's arrival.

sentences.zh: 金人聞之，夜斷河梁遁去。

translations.literal: The Jin heard of this and by night cut the river bridge and fled.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin heard of this, they cut the bridge by night and fled.

sentences.zh: 二年，金人自鄭抵白沙，去汴京密邇，都人震恐。

translations.literal: In the second year, the Jin came from Zheng to Baisha, very close to Bianjing; the capital's people were shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year the Jin advanced from Zheng to Baisha, very close to Bianjing, and the people of the capital were terrified.

sentences.zh: 僚屬入問計，澤方對客圍棋，笑曰：「何事張惶，劉衍等在外必能禦敵。

translations.literal: Staff entered to ask plans; Ze was just playing go with a guest and laughed: "Why be alarmed—Liu Yan and the others outside can surely repel the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: When his staff came in to ask for plans, Ze was playing go with a guest and laughed, "Why be alarmed? Liu Yan and the others outside can surely hold the enemy.

sentences.zh: 」乃選精銳數千，使繞出敵後，伏其歸路。

translations.literal: " He then selected several thousand elite troops to circle behind the enemy and ambush their line of retreat.
translations.idiomatic: He selected several thousand elite troops to circle behind the enemy and ambush their retreat.

sentences.zh: 金人方與衍戰，伏兵起，前後夾擊之，金人果敗。

translations.literal: The Jin were just fighting Yan when the ambush rose, striking them front and rear—the Jin were indeed defeated.
translations.idiomatic: While the Jin were fighting Liu Yan, the ambush rose and struck them from front and rear, and the Jin were defeated.

sentences.zh: 金將黏罕據西京，與澤相持。

translations.literal: Jin general Nianhan held the Western Capital and faced Ze in stalemate.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Nianhan held the Western Capital and faced Ze in stalemate.

sentences.zh: 澤遣部將李景良、閻中立、郭俊民領兵趨鄭，遇敵大戰，中立死之，俊民降，景良遁去。

translations.literal: Ze sent subordinates Li Jingliang, Yan Zhongli, and Guo Junmin leading troops toward Zheng; they met the enemy in great battle—Zhongli died, Junmin surrendered, Jingliang fled.
translations.idiomatic: Ze sent Li Jingliang, Yan Zhongli, and Guo Junmin toward Zheng. They met the enemy in a great battle; Yan Zhongli was killed, Guo Junmin surrendered, and Li Jingliang fled.

sentences.zh: 澤捕得景良，謂曰：「不勝，罪可恕；

translations.literal: Ze captured Jingliang and said: "Not winning—your crime may be forgiven;
translations.idiomatic: Ze captured Li Jingliang and said, "To lose a battle may be forgiven,

sentences.zh: 私自逃，是無主將也。

translations.literal: to flee on your own is to have no commander.
translations.idiomatic: but to flee on your own is to abandon your commander.

sentences.zh: 」斬其首以徇。

translations.literal: " He cut off his head and displayed it as warning.
translations.idiomatic: He had him beheaded and displayed the head as a warning.

sentences.zh: 既而俊民與金將史姓者及燕人何仲祖等持書來招澤，澤數俊民曰：「汝失利死，尚為忠義鬼，今反為金人持書相誘，何面目見我乎。

translations.literal: Soon Junmin with a Jin general surnamed Shi and the Yan man He Zhongzu and others came bearing letters to entice Ze; Ze reproached Junmin: "Had you died in defeat you would still be a loyal ghost—now you carry letters for the Jin to lure me; what face have you to see me?
translations.idiomatic: Soon Guo Junmin came with a Jin general surnamed Shi and the Yan man He Zhongzu, bearing letters to entice Ze. Ze reproached Junmin: "Had you died in defeat you would still be a loyal ghost—now you carry the Jin's letters to lure me. What face have you to see me?"

sentences.zh: 」斬之，謂史曰：「我受此土，有死而已。

translations.literal: " He executed him, and said to Shi: "I received this land—only death awaits.
translations.idiomatic: He executed Guo Junmin and said to the Jin general Shi, "I received this land from the Song—death is all I owe.

sentences.zh: 汝為人將，不能以死敵我，乃欲以兒女子語誘我乎。

translations.literal: You are a man's general—unable to meet me in death, you wish to entice me with women's and children's words?
translations.idiomatic: You are a general—unable to face me in battle, you would entice me with women's pleading?

sentences.zh: 」亦斬之。

translations.literal: " He executed him too.
translations.idiomatic: He executed him as well.

sentences.zh: 謂仲祖脅從，貸之。

translations.literal: He said Zhongzu was coerced and pardoned him.
translations.idiomatic: He said He Zhongzu had been coerced and spared him.

sentences.zh: 劉衍還，金人復入滑，部將張捴請往救，澤選兵五千付之，戒毋輕戰以需援。

translations.literal: Liu Yan returned; the Jin again entered Hua; subordinate Zhang Zhe asked to go rescue; Ze selected five thousand troops and gave them to him, warning not to fight lightly but await relief.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yan returned, the Jin again entered Hua. Subordinate Zhang Zhe asked to go to the rescue. Ze gave him five thousand troops and warned him not to fight rashly but to await reinforcements.

sentences.zh: 捴至滑迎戰，敵騎十倍，諸將請少避其鋒，捴曰：「避而偷生，何面目見宗公。

translations.literal: Zhe reached Hua and met battle; enemy cavalry were tenfold; the generals asked to yield a little before their edge; Zhe said: "To yield and steal life—what face to see Lord Zong?
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhe reached Hua and gave battle. The enemy cavalry outnumbered his force ten to one, and his officers urged him to withdraw. Zhang Zhe said, "To flee and live on—what face would I have to see Lord Zong?"

sentences.zh: 」力戰死之。

translations.literal: " He fought fiercely and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fought to the death.

sentences.zh: 澤聞捴急，遣王宣領騎五千救之。

translations.literal: Ze heard Zhe was in peril and sent Wang Xuan leading five thousand cavalry to rescue him.
translations.idiomatic: When Ze heard Zhang Zhe was in peril, he sent Wang Xuan with five thousand cavalry to rescue him.

sentences.zh: 捴死二日，宣始至，與金人大戰，破走之。

translations.literal: Two days after Zhe died, Xuan finally arrived, fought a great battle with the Jin, and routed them.
translations.idiomatic: Two days after Zhang Zhe died, Wang Xuan arrived, fought a great battle with the Jin, and routed them.

sentences.zh: 澤迎捴喪歸，恤其家，以宣權知滑州，金人自是不復犯東京。

translations.literal: Ze met Zhe's coffin returning, comforted his family, and made Xuan acting prefect of Hua—the Jin from then on no longer invaded the Eastern Capital.
translations.idiomatic: Ze met Zhang Zhe's coffin on its return, comforted his family, and appointed Wang Xuan acting prefect of Hua. From then on the Jin no longer attacked the Eastern Capital.

sentences.zh: 山東盜起，執政謂其多以義師為名，請下令止勤王。

translations.literal: Bandits rose in Shandong; the chief ministers said many used the name of loyalist armies and asked to issue an order stopping loyalist relief.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in Shandong, the chief ministers said many were using the name of loyalist armies and asked for an order forbidding loyalist relief forces.

sentences.zh: 澤疏曰：「自敵圍京城，忠義之士憤懣爭奮，廣之東西、湖之南北、福建、江、淮，越數千里，爭先勤王。

translations.literal: Ze memorialized: "Since the enemy besieged the capital, loyal men in indignant zeal strove forward—from east and west of Guang, north and south of the lakes, Fujian, Jiang, and Huai, crossing thousands of li, all vied to relieve the throne.
translations.idiomatic: Ze memorialized: "Since the enemy besieged the capital, loyal men have rushed forward in righteous anger from Guangdong and Guangxi, Hunan and Hubei, Fujian, Jiangnan, and Huai—crossing thousands of li to relieve the throne.

sentences.zh: 當時大臣無遠識大略，不能撫而用之，使之饑餓困窮，弱者填溝壑，強者為盜賊。

translations.literal: At that time great ministers lacked far vision and broad strategy, could not soothe and employ them, letting them hunger and be destitute—the weak filled ditches and ravines, the strong became bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers of that day lacked vision and could not organize and employ them, so they starved and suffered—the weak filled the ditches and ravines, the strong became bandits.

sentences.zh: 此非勤王者之罪，乃一時措置乖謬所致耳。

translations.literal: This is not the crime of those who relieved the throne—it was caused by mistaken arrangements of the moment.
translations.idiomatic: This was not the fault of the loyalists—it was caused by the court's mistaken policies of the day.

sentences.zh: 今河東、西不從敵國而保山砦者，不知其幾；

translations.literal: Now in Hedong and Hexi those who do not follow the enemy state but hold mountain stockades—one knows not how many;
translations.idiomatic: Today in Hedong and Hexi countless men hold mountain stockades rather than submit to the enemy;

sentences.zh: 諸處節義之夫，自黥其面而爭先救駕者，復不知其幾。

translations.literal: men of integrity everywhere who tattoo their faces and vie to rescue the sovereign—again one knows not how many.
translations.idiomatic: and everywhere men of integrity tattoo their faces and vie to rescue the sovereign—again, who can count them?

sentences.zh: 此詔一出，臣恐草澤之士一旦解體，倉卒有急，誰復有願忠效義之心哉。」

translations.literal: Once this edict issues, I fear men of the grasslands and marshes will dissolve at once; if sudden peril comes, who will again have hearts willing loyalty and righteousness?"
translations.idiomatic: Once this edict is issued, I fear the loyalists of the countryside will dissolve at once. If sudden peril comes, who will again have the heart to serve with loyalty and righteousness?"

sentences.zh: 王策者，本遼酋，為金將，往來河上。

translations.literal: Wang Ce was originally a Khitan chieftain, became a Jin general, and traveled along the river.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ce had been a Khitan chieftain and became a Jin general, traveling along the river.

sentences.zh: 澤擒之，解其縛坐堂上，為言：「契丹本宋兄弟之國，今女真辱吾主，又滅爾國，義當協謀雪恥。

translations.literal: Ze captured him, untied his bonds and seated him in the hall, saying: "The Khitan were originally Song's brother state; now the Jurchen shamed our sovereign and also destroyed your state—you should join in plotting to wipe away shame.
translations.idiomatic: Ze captured him, untied his bonds, seated him in the hall, and said, "The Khitan were once brothers to the Song. Now the Jurchen have shamed our sovereign and destroyed your state as well. By right we should join in plotting revenge.

sentences.zh: 」策感泣，願效死。

translations.literal: " Ce was moved to tears and wished to die in service.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Ce wept and vowed to serve unto death.

sentences.zh: 澤因問敵國虛實，盡得其詳，遂決大舉之計，召諸將謂曰：「汝等有忠義心，當協謀剿敵，期還二聖，以立大功。

translations.literal: Ze thereupon asked the enemy state's condition in detail, learned all particulars, and decided on a great campaign plan; summoning the generals he said: "You have loyal hearts—you should join in plotting to exterminate the enemy, hoping to return the two sage emperors and achieve great merit.
translations.idiomatic: Ze questioned him about the enemy's condition in detail, learned everything, and decided on a major campaign. Summoning his generals he said, "You have loyal hearts—join in plotting to destroy the enemy, recover the two emperors, and win great merit.

sentences.zh: 」言訖泣下，諸將皆泣聽命。

translations.literal: " When he finished speaking tears fell; all the generals wept as they received orders.
translations.idiomatic: When he finished speaking he wept, and all the generals wept as they received his orders.

sentences.zh: 金人戰不利，悉引兵去。

translations.literal: The Jin fought unfavorably and withdrew all troops.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin fared poorly in battle, they withdrew all their troops.

sentences.zh: 澤疏諫南幸，言：「臣為陛下保護京城，自去年秋冬至於今春，又三月矣。

translations.literal: Ze memorialized remonstrating against southern progress, saying: "This subject has protected the capital for Your Majesty—from last autumn and winter until this spring, another three months.
translations.idiomatic: Ze memorialized against the southern tour, saying, "I have protected the capital for Your Majesty—from last autumn and winter until this spring, three more months.

sentences.zh: 陛下不早回京城，則天下之民何所依戴。

translations.literal: If Your Majesty does not soon return to the capital, upon what will the people under Heaven rely and look up?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty does not soon return to the capital, upon whom will the people of the empire rely?"

sentences.zh: 」除資政殿學士。

translations.literal: " He was appointed academician of the Zizheng Hall.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed academician of the Zizheng Hall.

sentences.zh: 又遣子穎詣行闕上疏曰：「天下之事，見機而為，待時而動，則事無不成。

translations.literal: He also sent his son Ying to the traveling palace to memorialize: "Affairs under Heaven—act when you see the moment, move when you await the time—then nothing fails.
translations.idiomatic: He also sent his son Ying to the traveling palace to memorialize: "In affairs under Heaven, act when you see the moment and move when the time is ripe, and nothing will fail.

sentences.zh: 今收復伊、洛而金酋渡河，捍蔽滑台而敵國屢敗，河東、河北山砦義民，引領舉踵，日望官兵之至。

translations.literal: Now recovering Yi and Luo while the Jin chief crosses the river, shielding Huatai while the enemy state is repeatedly defeated, Hedong and Hebei mountain stockade loyal militia stretch their necks and stand on tiptoe, daily hoping for government troops to arrive.
translations.idiomatic: We have recovered Yi and Luo while the Jin chieftain crosses the river; we hold Huatai while the enemy suffers repeated defeats; the loyal militia of the mountain stockades of Hedong and Hebei stretch their necks daily awaiting the arrival of government troops.

sentences.zh: 以機以時而言之，中興之兆可見，而金人滅亡之期可必，在陛下見機乘時而已。

translations.literal: Speaking by moment and time, the omen of restoration is visible, and the Jin's day of extinction is certain—it rests only on Your Majesty seeing the moment and seizing the time.
translations.idiomatic: Judging by moment and time, the omen of restoration is visible and the day of the Jin's destruction is certain—it rests only on Your Majesty seizing the moment.

sentences.zh: 」又言：「昔楚人城郢，史氏鄙之。

translations.literal: " He also said: "In old days the Chu people walled Ying—the historians despised it.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "In antiquity when the Chu walled Ying, the historians despised it.

sentences.zh: 今聞有旨於儀真教習水戰，是規規為偏霸之謀，非可鄙之甚者乎？

translations.literal: Now I hear an edict to drill naval warfare at Yizhen—is this not scheming narrowly for regional hegemony, a thing most despicable?
translations.idiomatic: Now I hear an edict to drill naval warfare at Yizhen—is this not scheming narrowly for regional hegemony, a thing most despicable?

sentences.zh: 傳聞四方，必謂中原不守，遂為江寧控扼之計耳。」

translations.literal: Spread to the four quarters, all will surely say the Central Plain is not held, and this is only a plan to control and choke Jiangning."
translations.idiomatic: Spread abroad, all will say the Central Plain is abandoned and this is only a plan to fortify Jiangning."

sentences.zh: 先是，澤去磁，以州事付兵馬鈐轄李侃，統制趙世隆殺之。

translations.literal: Earlier, when Ze left Ci, he entrusted prefectural affairs to military commissioner Li Kan; commander Zhao Shilong killed him.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Ze left Cizhou he entrusted prefectural affairs to military commissioner Li Kan, whom commander Zhao Shilong killed.

sentences.zh: 至是，世隆及弟與興以兵三萬來歸，眾懼其變，澤曰：「世隆本吾一校爾，何能為。

translations.literal: At this time Shilong and his younger brother Yuxing came with thirty thousand troops to submit; the multitude feared mutiny; Ze said: "Shilong was originally just one of my sergeants—what can he do?
translations.idiomatic: At this time Zhao Shilong and his younger brother Yuxing came with thirty thousand troops to submit. The men feared treachery, but Ze said, "Shilong was originally just one of my sergeants—what can he do?"

sentences.zh: 」世隆至，責之曰：「河北陷沒，吾宋法令與上下之分亦陷沒邪？

translations.literal: " When Shilong arrived, Ze reproached him: "Hebei has fallen—have our Song laws and the distinction of superior and inferior also fallen?
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Shilong arrived, Ze reproached him: "Hebei has fallen—have the laws of the Song and the distinction between superior and subordinate fallen as well?"

sentences.zh: 」命斬之。

translations.literal: " He ordered him executed.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered him executed.

sentences.zh: 時世興佩刀侍側，眾兵露刃庭下，澤徐謂世興曰：「汝兄誅，汝能奮志立功，足以雪恥。

translations.literal: At that time Yuxing wore a sword attending at his side; soldiers bared blades in the courtyard; Ze slowly said to Yuxing: "Your elder brother is executed—you can rouse your will and achieve merit, enough to wipe away shame.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxing stood at his side with a sword, and soldiers bared their blades in the courtyard. Ze said calmly to Yuxing, "Your brother has been executed. If you rouse your will and win merit, you may wipe away this shame."

sentences.zh: 」世興感泣。

translations.literal: " Yuxing was moved to tears.
translations.idiomatic: Yuxing wept in gratitude.

sentences.zh: 金人攻滑州，澤遣世興往救，世興至，掩其不備，敗之。

translations.literal: The Jin attacked Hua prefecture; Ze sent Yuxing to rescue; Yuxing arrived, took them unawares, and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked Hua prefecture, Ze sent Yuxing to the rescue. Yuxing arrived, took them by surprise, and defeated them.

sentences.zh: 澤威聲日著，北方聞其名，常尊憚之，對南人言，必曰宗爺爺。

translations.literal: Ze's martial prestige grew daily; in the north when they heard his name they always honored and feared him; speaking to southerners they always said Grandfather Zong.
translations.idiomatic: Zong Ze's reputation grew daily. In the north, when people heard his name they honored and feared him, and speaking to southerners they always called him Grandfather Zong.

sentences.zh: 澤疏言：「丁進數十萬眾願守護京城，李成願扈從還闕，即渡河剿敵，楊進等兵百萬，亦願渡河，同致死力。

translations.literal: Ze memorialized: "Ding Jin's several hundred thousand wish to guard the capital; Li Cheng wishes to escort Your Majesty back to court and at once cross the river to exterminate the enemy; Yang Jin and others' million troops also wish to cross the river and together give their utmost strength.
translations.idiomatic: Ze memorialized: "Ding Jin commands several hundred thousand men who wish to guard the capital; Li Cheng wishes to escort Your Majesty back to court and cross the river at once to destroy the enemy; Yang Jin and others command a million men who also wish to cross the river and fight with all their strength.

sentences.zh: 臣聞'多助之至，天下順之'。

translations.literal: This subject has heard 'when help is abundant, all under Heaven follows.'
translations.idiomatic: I have heard that when help is abundant, all under Heaven follows.

sentences.zh: 陛下及此時還京，則眾心翕然，何敵國之足憂乎？

translations.literal: If Your Majesty seizes this time to return to the capital, then popular hearts will unite—what enemy state is worth worry?
translations.idiomatic: If Your Majesty returns to the capital now, the people's hearts will unite—what enemy need we fear?"

sentences.zh: 」又奏言：「聖人愛其親以及人之親，所以教人孝；

translations.literal: " He also memorialized: "The sage loves his kin and extends it to others' kin—thus he teaches filial piety;
translations.idiomatic: He also memorialized: "The sage loves his own kin and extends that love to others' kin—thus he teaches filial piety;

sentences.zh: 敬其兄以及人之兄，所以教人弟。

translations.literal: reveres his elder brother and extends it to others' elder brothers—thus he teaches brotherly duty.
translations.idiomatic: he reveres his elder brother and extends that reverence to others' elder brothers—thus he teaches brotherly duty.

sentences.zh: 陛下當與忠臣義士合謀肆討，迎復二聖。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should join loyal ministers and righteous men in plotting a great punitive campaign to welcome back the two sage emperors.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should join loyal ministers and righteous men in planning a great campaign to recover the two emperors.

sentences.zh: 今上皇所御龍德宮儼然如舊，惟淵聖皇帝未有宮室。

translations.literal: Now the Retired Emperor's Longde Palace stands as before; only the Profound Sage Emperor has no palace quarters.
translations.idiomatic: The Retired Emperor's Longde Palace stands as before, but the Profound Sage Emperor has no palace quarters.

sentences.zh: 望改修寶籙宮以為迎奉之所，使天下知孝于父、弟于兄，是以身教也。

translations.literal: I hope the Baolu Palace may be renovated as a place to welcome and receive them, so all under Heaven knows filial piety toward father and brotherly duty toward elder brother—this is teaching by personal example.
translations.idiomatic: I beg that the Baolu Palace be renovated as a place to receive them, so that all under Heaven may see filial piety toward father and brotherly duty toward elder brother—teaching by your own example."

sentences.zh: 」上乃降詔擇日還京。

translations.literal: " The emperor then issued an edict choosing a day to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then issued an edict choosing a day to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 澤前後請上還京二十餘奏，每為潛善等所抑，憂憤成疾，疽發於背。

translations.literal: Ze before and after submitted more than twenty memorials asking the emperor to return to the capital; each was suppressed by Qian Shan and others; worry and indignation became illness, and a carbuncle broke out on his back.
translations.idiomatic: Ze had submitted more than twenty memorials urging the emperor to return to the capital, each blocked by Huang Qianshan and his faction. Worry and indignation brought on illness, and a carbuncle broke out on his back.

sentences.zh: 諸將入問疾，澤矍然曰：「吾以二帝蒙塵，積憤至此。

translations.literal: The generals entered to inquire after his illness; Ze started awake and said: "Because the two emperors suffer dust and dishonor, accumulated indignation has reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals came to inquire after his illness, Ze said with a start, "Because the two emperors suffer disgrace, my indignation has brought me to this.

sentences.zh: 汝等能殲敵，則我死無恨。

translations.literal: If you can exterminate the enemy, then my death will be without regret.
translations.idiomatic: If you can destroy the enemy, I shall die without regret.

sentences.zh: 」眾皆流涕曰：「敢不盡力！

translations.literal: " All wept and said: "How dare we not exert our utmost!
translations.idiomatic: All wept and said, "How could we fail to exert our utmost!"

sentences.zh: 」諸將出，澤歎曰：「'出師未捷身先死，長使英雄淚滿襟。

translations.literal: " When the generals left, Ze sighed: "'The army went forth without victory and the body died first—forever making heroes' tears fill their collars.
translations.idiomatic: When the generals left, Ze sighed, "'The army went forth without victory and the body died first—forever making heroes' tears fill their collars.'"

sentences.zh: '」翌日，風雨晝晦。

translations.literal: '" The next day, wind and rain darkened the day.
translations.idiomatic: The next day wind and rain darkened the sky.

sentences.zh: 澤無一語及家事，但連呼「過河」者三而薨。

translations.literal: Ze spoke not a word of household affairs, but thrice cried "Cross the river!" and died.
translations.idiomatic: Ze spoke not a word of household affairs, but thrice cried "Cross the river!" and died.

sentences.zh: 都人號慟。

translations.literal: The capital's people wailed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: The people of the capital wailed in grief.

sentences.zh: 遺表猶贊上還京。

translations.literal: His final memorial still urged the emperor to return to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: His final memorial still urged the emperor to return to the capital.

sentences.zh: 贈觀文殿學士、通議大夫，諡忠簡。

translations.literal: He was posthumously given Guanwen Hall academician and Grand Master of Discussion; his posthumous name was Zhongjian (Loyal and Simple).
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously given the titles of Guanwen Hall academician and Grand Master of Discussion, with the posthumous name Zhongjian (Loyal and Simple).

sentences.zh: 澤質直好義，親故貧者多依以為活，而自奉甚薄。

translations.literal: Ze was plain and upright, fond of righteousness; many poor kin and friends relied on him to live, while his own provisions were very spare.
translations.idiomatic: Ze was plainspoken and righteous; many poor relatives and friends relied on him for their livelihood, while he lived very frugally himself.

sentences.zh: 常曰：「君父側身嘗膽，臣子乃安居美食邪！

translations.literal: He often said: "The sovereign and father sleeps on brushwood and tastes gall—how can subjects dwell at ease and feast on delicacies!
translations.idiomatic: He often said, "While the sovereign sleeps on brushwood and tastes gall, how can a subject live at ease and feast on delicacies!"

sentences.zh: 」始，澤詔集群盜，聚兵儲糧，結諸路義兵，連燕、趙豪傑，自謂渡河克復可指日冀。

translations.literal: " At first Ze gathered bandits by edict, amassed troops and stored grain, joined loyalist armies of all circuits, linked Yan and Zhao heroes—he himself thought crossing the river to recover territory could be hoped for within days.
translations.idiomatic: At first Ze gathered the bandit chiefs by edict, amassed troops and stored grain, joined loyalist armies from every circuit, and linked the heroes of Yan and Zhao. He believed that crossing the river to recover the north could be achieved within days.

sentences.zh: 有志弗就，識者恨之。

translations.literal: His ambition was not fulfilled—those who knew him regretted it.
translations.idiomatic: His ambition was not fulfilled, and those who knew him mourned it.

sentences.zh: 子穎，居戎幕，素得士心。

translations.literal: His son Ying dwelt in the military camp and had always won soldiers' hearts.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ying served in the military camp and had always won the soldiers' hearts.

sentences.zh: 澤薨數日，將士去者十五，都人請以穎繼父任。

translations.literal: Several days after Ze died, five-tenths of officers and soldiers departed; the capital's people asked that Ying succeed his father's post.
translations.idiomatic: Within days of Ze's death half the officers and soldiers departed, and the people of the capital asked that Ying succeed his father's post.

sentences.zh: 會朝廷已命杜充留守，乃以穎為判官。

translations.literal: Just then the court had already appointed Du Chong garrison commander, so Ying was made adjutant.
translations.idiomatic: The court had already appointed Du Chong as garrison commander, so Ying was made adjutant.

sentences.zh: 充反澤所為，頗失人心，穎屢爭之，不從，乃請持服歸。

translations.literal: Chong reversed what Ze had done and greatly lost popular hearts; Ying repeatedly argued but was not obeyed, and asked to return home in mourning dress.
translations.idiomatic: Du Chong reversed Ze's policies and lost the people's hearts. Ying repeatedly protested but was ignored, and asked to return home to observe mourning.

sentences.zh: 自是豪傑不為用，群聚城下者復去為盜，而中原不守矣。

translations.literal: From then on heroes were not employed; those who had gathered below the walls again left to become bandits—and the Central Plain was not held.
translations.idiomatic: From then on the heroes were not employed; those who had gathered below the walls returned to banditry, and the Central Plain was lost.

sentences.zh: 穎官終兵部郎中。

translations.literal: Ying ended his career as Director in the Ministry of War.
translations.idiomatic: Ying ended his career as Director in the Ministry of War.

sentences.zh: 趙鼎，字元鎮，解州聞喜人。

translations.literal: Zhao Ding, courtesy name Yuanzhen, was a native of Wenxi in Jie prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding, courtesy name Yuanzhen, was from Wenxi in Jie prefecture.

sentences.zh: 生四歲而孤，母樊教之，通經史百家之書。

translations.literal: He lost his father at four; his mother Fan taught him, and he mastered the classics, histories, and the books of the hundred schools.
translations.idiomatic: He lost his father at four. His mother Fan taught him, and he mastered the classics, histories, and the books of the hundred schools.

sentences.zh: 登崇甯五年進士第，對策斥章惇誤國。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the fifth year of Chongning; in the policy response he denounced Zhang Dun for harming the state.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in 1106 (the fifth year of the Chongning reign) and in his policy response denounced Zhang Dun for harming the state.

sentences.zh: 累官為河南洛陽令，宰相吳敏和其能，擢為開封士曹。

translations.literal: Through successive offices he became magistrate of Luoyang in Henan; Chief Councillor Wu Min praised his ability and promoted him to Kaifeng legal officer.
translations.idiomatic: He rose through successive offices to magistrate of Luoyang in Henan. Chief Councillor Wu Min praised his ability and promoted him to legal officer of Kaifeng.
