sentences.zh: 金人陷太原，朝廷議割三鎮地，鼎曰：「祖宗之地不可以與人，何庸議？

translations.literal: The Jin took Taiyuan; the court discussed ceding the three prefectures' territory; Ding said: "The ancestral founders' lands cannot be given to others—why discuss it?
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin captured Taiyuan and the court discussed ceding the three prefectures, Ding said, "The lands of our ancestral founders cannot be given away—why even discuss it?"

sentences.zh: 」已而京師失守，二帝北行。

translations.literal: " Soon the capital fell; the two emperors went north.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the capital fell and both emperors were taken north.

sentences.zh: 金人議立張邦昌，鼎與胡寅、張浚逃太學中，不書議狀。

translations.literal: The Jin discussed enthroning Zhang Bangchang; Ding with Hu Yin and Zhang Jun fled into the Imperial Academy and did not sign the deliberation document.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin discussed enthroning Zhang Bangchang, Ding fled with Hu Yin and Zhang Jun into the Imperial Academy and refused to sign the deliberation document.

sentences.zh: 久雨，詔求闕政。

translations.literal: After long rain, an edict sought governmental shortcomings.
translations.idiomatic: After prolonged rain, an edict sought reports of governmental shortcomings.

sentences.zh: 鼎言：「自熙寧間王安石用事，變祖宗之法，而民始病。

translations.literal: Ding said: "From the Xining era when Wang Anshi held power, he changed the ancestral founders' laws, and the people first suffered.
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "From the Xining era, when Wang Anshi held power, he changed the laws of the ancestral founders, and the people first began to suffer.

sentences.zh: 假辟國之謀，造生邊患；

translations.literal: using schemes of territorial expansion, he created border troubles;
translations.idiomatic: Using schemes of territorial expansion, he created border troubles;

sentences.zh: 興理財之政，窮困民力；

translations.literal: launching revenue policies, he exhausted the people's strength;
translations.idiomatic: launching revenue policies, he exhausted the people's strength;

sentences.zh: 設虛無之學，敗壞人才。

translations.literal: establishing empty learning, he ruined talent.
translations.idiomatic: establishing empty learning, he ruined talent.

sentences.zh: 至崇甯初，蔡京托紹述之名，盡祖安石之政。

translations.literal: By the beginning of Chongning, Cai Jing under the name of continuing the legacy wholly adopted Wang Anshi's policies.
translations.idiomatic: By the beginning of the Chongning reign, Cai Jing under the name of continuing the legacy wholly adopted Wang Anshi's policies.

sentences.zh: 凡今日之患始于安石，成于蔡京。

translations.literal: All of today's troubles began with Anshi and were completed by Cai Jing.
translations.idiomatic: All of today's troubles began with Wang Anshi and were completed by Cai Jing.

sentences.zh: 今安石猶配享廟廷，而京之黨未除，時政之闕無大於此。

translations.literal: Now Anshi still shares sacrifice in the temple court, while Jing's faction is not removed—no governmental shortcoming is greater than this.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Anshi still shares sacrifice in the temple court, while Cai Jing's faction is not removed—no governmental shortcoming is greater than this."

sentences.zh: 」上為罷安石配享。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon abolished Anshi's shared sacrifice.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon abolished Wang Anshi's shared sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 擢右司諫，旋遷殿中侍御史。

translations.literal: He was promoted to Right Bureau remonstrator, then soon transferred to Palace Attendant Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Right Bureau remonstrator, then soon transferred to Palace Attendant Censor.

sentences.zh: 劉光世部將王德擅殺韓世忠之將，而世忠亦率部曲奪建康守府廨。

translations.literal: Liu Guangshi's subordinate Wang De arbitrarily killed one of Han Shizhong's generals, while Shizhong also led his personal troops to seize the Jiankang prefect's offices.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangshi's subordinate Wang De arbitrarily killed one of Han Shizhong's generals, while Han Shizhong also led his personal troops to seize the Jiankang prefect's offices.

sentences.zh: 鼎言：「德總兵在外，專殺無忌，此而不治，孰不可為？

translations.literal: Ding said: "De commands troops outside and kills at will without restraint—if this is not punished, what cannot be done?
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "Wang De commands troops in the field and kills at will without restraint—if this is not punished, what cannot be done?"

sentences.zh: 」命鼎鞫德。

translations.literal: " He ordered Ding to try De.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor ordered Ding to try Wang De.

sentences.zh: 鼎又請下詔切責世忠，而指取其將吏付有司治罪，諸將肅然。

translations.literal: Ding also asked to issue an edict sternly reproaching Shizhong, and to take out his generals and officials for punishment by the authorities—the generals were all awed.
translations.idiomatic: Ding also asked for an edict sternly reproaching Han Shizhong and for his generals and officials to be handed over for punishment. The generals were all awed.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「肅宗興靈武得一李勉，朝廷始尊。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When Suzong rose at Lingwu and gained one Li Mian, the court first gained respect.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When Emperor Suzong rose at Lingwu and gained Li Mian, the court first gained respect.

sentences.zh: 今朕得卿，無愧昔人矣。

translations.literal: Now I have gained you—I am not shamed before the men of old."
translations.idiomatic: Now I have gained you—I need not be shamed before the men of old."

sentences.zh: 」中丞范宗尹言，故事無自司諫遷殿中者，上曰：「鼎在言路極舉職，所言四十事，已施行三十有六。

translations.literal: " Censor Fan Zongyin said precedent had no transfer from Bureau remonstrator to Palace Attendant; the emperor said: "Ding on the remonstrance path has extremely fulfilled his office—the forty matters he spoke of, thirty-six have already been carried out.
translations.idiomatic: Censor Fan Zongyin said precedent had no transfer from Bureau remonstrator to Palace Attendant. The emperor said, "Ding has extremely fulfilled his office on the remonstrance path—of the forty matters he spoke of, thirty-six have already been carried out."

sentences.zh: 」遂遷侍御史。

translations.literal: " He was then transferred to Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was then transferred to Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 北兵至江上，上幸會稽，召台諫議去留，鼎陳戰、守、避三策，拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: Northern troops reached the river; the emperor visited Kuaiji; he summoned censors and remonstrators to discuss staying or leaving; Ding set forth three strategies—fight, defend, flee—and was appointed Censor-in-Chief.
translations.idiomatic: When northern troops reached the Yangtze, the emperor visited Kuaiji and summoned the censors and remonstrators to discuss staying or leaving. Ding set forth three strategies—fight, defend, or flee—and was appointed Censor-in-Chief.

sentences.zh: 請督王𤫉进軍宣州，周望分軍出廣德，劉光世渡江駐蘄、黃，為邀擊之計。

translations.literal: He asked to supervise Wang Yuan's advance on Xuanzhou, Zhou Wang's division out Guangde, Liu Guangshi crossing the river to garrison Qi and Huang—as a plan to intercept.
translations.idiomatic: He asked to supervise Wang Yuan's advance on Xuanzhou, Zhou Wang's division out of Guangde, and Liu Guangshi's crossing the river to garrison Qi and Huang as a plan to intercept the enemy.

sentences.zh: 又言：「經營中原當自關中始，經營關中當自蜀始，欲幸蜀當自荊、襄始。

translations.literal: He also said: "Managing the Central Plain should begin from Guanzhong; managing Guanzhong should begin from Shu; wishing to visit Shu should begin from Jing and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "Recovering the Central Plain must begin from Guanzhong; recovering Guanzhong must begin from Shu; and reaching Shu must begin from Jing and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 吳、越介在一隅，非進取中原之地。

translations.literal: Wu and Yue lie in a corner—it is not land for advancing on the Central Plain.
translations.idiomatic: Wu and Yue lie in a corner—they are not a base from which to advance on the Central Plain.

sentences.zh: 荊、襄左顧川、陝，右控湖湘，而下瞰京、洛，三國所必爭，宜以公安為行闕，而屯重兵於襄陽，運江、浙之粟以資川、陝之兵，經營大業，計無出此。」

translations.literal: Jing and Xiang look left to Chuan and Shan, control right Hu and Xiang, and look down on Jing and Luo—the Three Kingdoms' necessary contest; Gong'an should be the traveling palace, heavy troops garrisoned at Xiangyang, transporting Jiang and Zhe grain to supply Chuan and Shan troops—managing the great enterprise, no plan surpasses this."
translations.idiomatic: Jing and Xiang look west to Sichuan and Shaanxi, control Hunan and Hubei to the east, and overlook Luoyang and the capital—the ground the Three Kingdoms always fought over. Gong'an should be the traveling palace, heavy troops should be garrisoned at Xiangyang, and grain from Jiangnan and Zhejiang should supply the armies of Sichuan and Shaanxi. For the great enterprise of recovery, no plan surpasses this."

sentences.zh: 韓世忠敗金人于黃天蕩，宰相呂頤浩請上幸浙西，下詔親征，鼎以為不可輕舉。

translations.literal: Han Shizhong defeated the Jin at Huangtiandang; Chief Councillor Lü Yihao asked the emperor to visit western Zhe, and an edict ordered a personal campaign—Ding thought one should not act rashly.
translations.idiomatic: When Han Shizhong defeated the Jin at Huangtiandang, Chief Councillor Lü Yihao urged the emperor to visit western Zhe and an edict ordered a personal campaign. Ding argued that such a move should not be made rashly.

sentences.zh: 頤浩惡其異己，改鼎翰林學士，鼎不拜，改吏部尚書，又不拜，言：「陛下有聽納之誠，而宰相陳拒諫之說；

translations.literal: Yihao resented his dissent, changed Ding to Hanlin academician—Ding did not accept; changed him to Minister of Personnel—again he did not accept, saying: "Your Majesty has the sincerity to listen and accept, while the chief councillor presents the doctrine of rejecting remonstrance;
translations.idiomatic: Yihao resented his dissent and transferred him to Hanlin academician—Ding refused to accept. He was then made Minister of Personnel—again he refused, saying, "Your Majesty has the sincerity to listen and accept counsel, while the chief councillor presents the doctrine of rejecting remonstrance;

sentences.zh: 陛下有眷待台臣之意，而宰相挾挫沮言官之威。

translations.literal: Your Majesty has the intent to cherish and treat censorial officials well, while the chief councillor wields the power to thwart and discourage remonstrating officials.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty intends to cherish the censorial officials, while the chief councillor wields the power to thwart and discourage them."

sentences.zh: 」堅臥不出，疏頤浩過失凡千言。

translations.literal: " He firmly lay abed and would not go out, memorializing Yihao's faults in altogether a thousand words.
translations.idiomatic: He firmly refused to take office and memorialized Yihao's faults in a memorial of a thousand words.

sentences.zh: 上罷頤浩，詔鼎復為中丞，謂鼎曰：「朕每聞前朝忠諫之臣，恨不之識，今於卿見之。

translations.literal: The emperor dismissed Yihao and ordered Ding restored as censor-in-chief, saying to Ding: "Whenever I hear of loyal remonstrating ministers of former dynasties, I regret not knowing them—now I see it in you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor dismissed Yihao and restored Ding as censor-in-chief, saying to him, "Whenever I hear of loyal remonstrating ministers of former dynasties, I regret not knowing them—now I see such a man in you."

sentences.zh: 」除端明殿學士、簽書樞密院事。

translations.literal: " He was appointed Duanming Hall academician and Privy Council signatory.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed Duanming Hall academician and Privy Council signatory.

sentences.zh: 金人攻楚州，鼎奏遣張俊往援之。

translations.literal: The Jin attacked Chuzhou; Ding memorialized sending Zhang Jun to relieve it.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin attacked Chuzhou, Ding memorialized sending Zhang Jun to relieve it.

sentences.zh: 俊不行，山陽遂陷，金人留淮上，范宗尹奏敵未必能再渡，鼎曰：「勿恃其不來，恃吾有以待之。

translations.literal: Jun would not go; Shanyang then fell; the Jin remained on the Huai; Fan Zongyin memorialized the enemy might not cross again—Ding said: "Do not rely on their not coming—rely on our having means to await them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun would not go, and Shanyang fell. The Jin remained on the Huai. Fan Zongyin memorialized that the enemy might not cross again. Ding said, "Do not rely on their not coming—rely on our being ready for them.

sentences.zh: 三省常以敵退為陛下援人才、修政事，密院常虞敵至為陛下申軍律、治甲兵，即兩得之。

translations.literal: The Three Departments always use enemy retreat for Your Majesty to draw talent and repair government; the Privy Council always fears enemy arrival to enforce military law and ready armor and weapons for Your Majesty—in both one gains.
translations.idiomatic: The Three Departments can use enemy retreat to draw talent and repair government for Your Majesty, while the Privy Council can use the fear of enemy arrival to enforce military law and ready arms—in both cases Your Majesty gains."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「卿等如此，朕復何憂。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "With you like this, what have I to worry about?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "With ministers like you, what have I to worry about?"

sentences.zh: 」鼎以楚州之失，上章丐去。

translations.literal: " Because of the loss of Chuzhou, Ding submitted a memorial begging to leave office.
translations.idiomatic: Because of the loss of Chuzhou, Ding submitted a memorial asking to leave office.

sentences.zh: 會辛企宗除節度使，鼎言企宗非軍功，忤旨，出奉祠，除知平江府，尋改知建康，又移知洪州。

translations.literal: Just then Xin Qizong was appointed military commissioner; Ding said Qizong had no military merit, offended the imperial intent, was sent out to temple service, appointed prefect of Pingjiang, soon changed to Jiankang, then transferred to Hongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: When Xin Qizong was appointed military commissioner, Ding said he had won no military merit. Offending the emperor, Ding was sent out to temple service, appointed prefect of Pingjiang, soon transferred to Jiankang, then to Hongzhou.

sentences.zh: 京西招撫使李橫欲用兵復東京，鼎言：「橫烏合之眾，不能當敵，恐遂失襄陽。

translations.literal: Western Jing pacification commissioner Li Heng wished to use troops to recover the Eastern Capital; Ding said: "Heng's mob-gathered host cannot match the enemy—I fear Xiangyang will then be lost.
translations.idiomatic: When Western Jing pacification commissioner Li Heng wished to use troops to recover the Eastern Capital, Ding said, "Li Heng's mob-gathered host cannot match the enemy—I fear we will lose Xiangyang."

sentences.zh: 」已而橫戰不利走，襄陽竟陷。

translations.literal: " Soon Heng fought unfavorably and fled—Xiangyang indeed fell.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Heng fought unfavorably and fled, and Xiangyang indeed fell.

sentences.zh: 召拜參知政事。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Vice Grand Councillor.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed Vice Grand Councillor.

sentences.zh: 宰相朱勝非言：「襄陽國之上流，不可不急取。

translations.literal: Chief Councillor Zhu Shengfei said: "Xiangyang is the state's upper stream—it cannot but be urgently retaken.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Councillor Zhu Shengfei said, "Xiangyang is the upper reach of the realm—it must be retaken urgently."

sentences.zh: 」上問：「岳飛可使否？

translations.literal: " The emperor asked: "Can Yue Fei be employed?
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Can Yue Fei be employed?"

sentences.zh: 」鼎曰：「知上流利害無如飛者。

translations.literal: " Ding said: "None knows the upper stream's advantages and harms like Fei.
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "No one knows the advantages and dangers of the upper stream like Yue Fei."

sentences.zh: 」簽樞徐俯不以為然。

translations.literal: " Privy Council signatory Xu Fu did not agree.
translations.idiomatic: Privy Council signatory Xu Fu did not agree.

sentences.zh: 飛出師竟復襄陽。

translations.literal: Fei led troops forth and indeed recovered Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: Yue Fei led his army forth and indeed recovered Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 鼎乞令韓世忠屯泗上，劉光世出陳、蔡。

translations.literal: Ding asked that Han Shizhong garrison Si prefecture and Liu Guangshi advance from Chen and Cai.
translations.idiomatic: Ding asked that Han Shizhong garrison Si prefecture and Liu Guangshi advance from Chen and Cai.

sentences.zh: 光世請入奏，俯欲許之，鼎不可。

translations.literal: Guangshi asked to enter and memorialize; Fu wished to permit it—Ding would not allow it.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangshi asked to enter court and memorialize. Xu Fu wished to permit it, but Ding would not allow it.

sentences.zh: 偽齊宿遷令來歸，俯欲斬送劉豫，鼎復爭之。

translations.literal: The false Qi's Suqian magistrate came to submit; Fu wished to execute and send him to Liu Yu—Ding again argued against it.
translations.idiomatic: When the puppet Qi's magistrate of Suqian came to submit, Xu Fu wished to execute him and send him to Liu Yu. Ding again argued against it.

sentences.zh: 俯積不能平，乃求去。

translations.literal: Fu's accumulated resentment could not be settled, and he asked to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Fu's resentment could not be settled, and he asked to leave office.

sentences.zh: 朱勝非兼知樞密院，言者謂當國者不知兵，乞令參政通知。

translations.literal: Zhu Shengfei concurrently managed the Privy Council; critics said those holding state power knew not military affairs and asked that the vice councillor be made aware.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei concurrently managed the Privy Council. Critics said those holding state power knew nothing of military affairs and asked that the vice councillor be put in charge of military affairs.

sentences.zh: 由是為勝非所忌。

translations.literal: Thereby he was resented by Shengfei.
translations.idiomatic: Thereby he came to be resented by Zhu Shengfei.

sentences.zh: 除鼎知樞密院、川陝宣撫使，鼎辭以非才。

translations.literal: Ding was appointed to manage the Privy Council and Sichuan-Shaanxi pacification commissioner; Ding declined on grounds of lacking talent.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was appointed to manage the Privy Council and made Sichuan–Shaanxi pacification commissioner. He declined on grounds of lacking talent.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「四川全盛半天下之地，盡以付卿，黜陟專之可也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Sichuan at full strength is half the land under Heaven—all is entrusted to you; appointments and dismissals may be yours alone.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Sichuan at full strength is half the land under Heaven—all is entrusted to you, and appointments and dismissals may be yours alone."

sentences.zh: 」時吳玠為宣撫副使，鼎奏言：「臣與玠同事，或節制之耶？

translations.literal: " At that time Wu Jie was deputy pacification commissioner; Ding memorialized: "This subject and Jie serve together—am I to control him?
translations.idiomatic: At that time Wu Jie was deputy pacification commissioner. Ding memorialized, "Wu Jie and I serve together—am I to control him?"

sentences.zh: 」上乃改鼎都督川、陝諸軍事。

translations.literal: " The emperor then changed Ding to overall commander of Sichuan and Shaanxi military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor then changed Ding's appointment to overall commander of Sichuan and Shaanxi military affairs.

sentences.zh: 鼎所條奏，勝非多沮抑之。

translations.literal: Of Ding's listed memorials, Shengfei mostly obstructed and suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: Zhu Shengfei mostly obstructed and suppressed Ding's memorials.

sentences.zh: 鼎上疏言：「頃張浚出使川、陝，國勢百倍於今。

translations.literal: Ding memorialized: "Recently Zhang Jun went as envoy to Chuan and Shan—the state's strength was a hundredfold today's.
translations.idiomatic: Ding memorialized: "When Zhang Jun recently went as envoy to Sichuan and Shaanxi, the state's strength was a hundredfold what it is today.

sentences.zh: 浚有補天浴日之功，陛下有礪山帶河之誓，君臣相信，古今無二，而終致物議，以被竄逐。

translations.literal: Jun had merit to mend heaven and bathe the sun; Your Majesty had an oath like grinding mountains and girdling rivers—sovereign and minister trusted each other, unmatched in ancient and modern times—yet in the end public criticism arose and he was banished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun had merit to mend heaven and bathe the sun; Your Majesty had sworn an oath as enduring as grinding mountains and girdling rivers. Sovereign and minister trusted each other as few have in history—yet in the end public criticism arose and he was banished.

sentences.zh: 今臣無浚之功而當其任，遠去朝廷，其能免於紛紛乎？

translations.literal: Now this subject has not Jun's merit yet holds his post, far from court—can I escape the clamor?
translations.idiomatic: Now I have not Zhang Jun's merit yet hold his post, far from court—how can I escape the clamor?"

sentences.zh: 」又言：「臣所請兵不滿數千，半皆老弱，所齎金帛至微，薦舉之人除命甫下，彈墨已行。

translations.literal: " He also said: "The troops I requested number less than a few thousand, half are old and weak, the gold and silk I carry are very slight—those I recommended, as soon as appointment orders issue, impeachment documents already proceed.
translations.idiomatic: He also wrote: "The troops I requested number less than a few thousand, half are old and weak, the gold and silk I carry are very slight—and those I recommended, as soon as appointment orders issue, impeachment documents already follow."

sentences.zh: 臣日侍宸衷，所陳已艱難，況在萬里之外乎？

translations.literal: This subject daily attends the imperial heart—what I state is already difficult; how much more ten thousand li away?
translations.idiomatic: Daily attendance at court is already difficult enough for what I must say—how much more from ten thousand li away?"

sentences.zh: 」時人士皆惜其去，台諫有留行者。

translations.literal: " At that time scholars and officials all regretted his going; censors and remonstrators petitioned to keep him.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars and officials all regretted his going, and censors and remonstrators petitioned to keep him.

sentences.zh: 會邊報遝至，鼎每陳用兵大計，及朝辭，上曰：「卿豈可遠去，當遂相卿。

translations.literal: Just then border reports arrived in succession; Ding each time set forth great military plans; at court farewell the emperor said: "How can you go far away—you should soon be chief councillor.
translations.idiomatic: Border reports then arrived in succession, and Ding each time set forth his great military plans. At his court farewell the emperor said, "How can you go so far away—you should soon be chief councillor."

sentences.zh: 」九月，拜尚書右僕射、同中書門下平章事兼知樞密院事。

translations.literal: " In the ninth month he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Concurrent Master of the Hall with Assent at the Secretariat-Chancellery Gate, and concurrent manager of the Privy Council.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was appointed Right Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Concurrent Master of the Hall with Assent at the Secretariat-Chancellery Gate, and concurrent manager of the Privy Council.

sentences.zh: 制下，朝士相慶。

translations.literal: When the appointment order issued, court officials congratulated one another.
translations.idiomatic: When the appointment was announced, court officials congratulated one another.

sentences.zh: 時劉豫子麟與金人合兵大入，舉朝震恐。

translations.literal: At that time Liu Yu's son Lin combined forces with the Jin and invaded on a great scale; the whole court was shaken with fear.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Liu Yu's son Lin combined forces with the Jin and launched a major invasion, throwing the entire court into alarm.

sentences.zh: 鼎論戰禦之計，諸將各異議，獨張俊以為當進討，鼎是其言。

translations.literal: Ding discussed plans for fighting and defense; the generals each had different views; only Zhang Jun held that they should advance and attack; Ding approved his words.
translations.idiomatic: Ding set forth plans for fighting off the invasion. The generals disagreed among themselves, but Zhang Jun alone argued they should advance and attack, and Ding agreed with him.

sentences.zh: 有勸上他幸者，鼎曰：「戰而不捷，去未晚也。

translations.literal: Some urged the emperor to take refuge elsewhere; Ding said: "If we fight and do not prevail, it will not be too late to leave.
translations.idiomatic: Some urged the emperor to flee elsewhere. Ding said, "If we fight and do not prevail, it will not be too late to leave."

sentences.zh: 」上亦曰：「朕當親總六師，臨江決戰。

translations.literal: " The emperor also said: "I shall personally command the Six Armies and fight a decisive battle at the river.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also said, "I shall personally take command of the armies and fight a decisive battle at the Yangzi."

sentences.zh: 」鼎喜曰：「累年退怯，敵志益驕，今聖斷親征，成功可必。

translations.literal: " Ding said joyfully: "Years of retreat and timidity have made the enemy ever prouder; now with the sacred decision to go in person, success is certain.
translations.idiomatic: Ding said with delight, "Years of retreat had made the enemy ever bolder. Now that Your Majesty has resolved to lead in person, victory is assured."

sentences.zh: 」於是詔張俊以所部援韓世忠，而命劉光世移軍建康，且促世忠進兵。

translations.literal: " Thereupon an edict ordered Zhang Jun to support Han Shizhong with his forces, commanded Liu Guangshi to move his army to Jiankang, and urged Han Shizhong to advance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered Zhang Jun to reinforce Han Shizhong with his troops, Liu Guangshi to move his army to Jiankang, and Han Shizhong to advance without delay.

sentences.zh: 世忠至揚州，大破金人於大儀鎮。

translations.literal: Shizhong reached Yangzhou and routed the Jin at Dayi town.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong reached Yangzhou and routed the Jin at Dayi.

sentences.zh: 方警報交馳，劉光世遣人諷鼎曰：「相公自入蜀，何事為他人任患。

translations.literal: Just as urgent reports were arriving in rapid succession, Liu Guangshi sent someone to hint to Ding: "Since the chief councillor entered Shu himself, why bear troubles for others?
translations.idiomatic: As urgent reports poured in, Liu Guangshi sent a messenger to hint to Ding, "The chief councillor once fled into Shu himself—why take on risks for others now?"

sentences.zh: 」世忠亦謂人曰：「趙丞相真敢為者。

translations.literal: " Shizhong also said to others: "Chief Councillor Zhao is truly a man who dares act.
translations.idiomatic: Han Shizhong also remarked, "Chief Councillor Zhao is truly a man who dares to act."

sentences.zh: 」鼎聞之，恐上意中變，乘間言：「陛下養兵十年，用之正在今日。

translations.literal: " When Ding heard this, fearing the emperor's mind might change midway, he seized an opportunity to say: "Your Majesty has trained troops for ten years—today is precisely the day to use them.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding heard this, fearing the emperor might change his mind, he seized a moment to say, "Your Majesty has trained troops for ten years—the time to use them is now."

sentences.zh: 若少加退沮，即人心渙散，長江之險不可復恃矣。

translations.literal: If we show the slightest retreat or discouragement, hearts will at once scatter, and the Yangzi's natural barrier can no longer be relied upon.
translations.idiomatic: The slightest show of retreat will scatter men's hearts, and we can no longer rely on the Yangzi as our barrier."

sentences.zh: 」及捷音日至，車駕至平江，下詔聲逆豫之罪，欲自將渡江決戰。

translations.literal: " As victory reports arrived daily, the imperial carriage reached Pingjiang; an edict was issued proclaiming Liu Yu's crimes, and the emperor wished to lead the crossing of the river himself for a decisive battle.
translations.idiomatic: When victory reports arrived daily, the emperor reached Pingjiang, issued an edict denouncing Liu Yu's crimes, and wished to cross the river and lead the decisive battle himself.

sentences.zh: 鼎曰：「敵之遠來，利於速戰，遽與爭鋒，非策也。

translations.literal: Ding said: "The enemy came from afar and gains from quick battle—hastily to cross swords with them is not sound strategy.
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "The enemy came from far away and gains from a quick battle. To rush into a clash is poor strategy."

sentences.zh: 且豫猶遣其子，豈可煩至尊耶？

translations.literal: Moreover, it is still Liu Yu who sent his son—how can we trouble the Son of Heaven?
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, it is only Liu Yu who sent his son—why must Your Majesty go to the trouble?"

sentences.zh: 」帝為止不行。

translations.literal: " The emperor on this account stopped and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor thereupon abandoned the plan and did not go.

sentences.zh: 未幾，簽書樞密院事胡松年自江上還，云北兵大集，然後知鼎之有先見也。

translations.literal: Before long, Vice Privy Councillor Hu Songnian returned from the river front and reported that northern troops were gathering in force—only then did they know Ding had foresight.
translations.idiomatic: Before long, Vice Privy Councillor Hu Songnian returned from the river front and reported that northern troops were massing in force, and all then saw that Ding had foreseen it.

sentences.zh: 張浚久廢，鼎言浚可大任，乃召除知樞密院，命浚往江上視師。

translations.literal: Zhang Jun had long been dismissed; Ding said Jun could be greatly entrusted; he was summoned and appointed to manage the Privy Council, and ordered to go to the river front to oversee the armies.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun had long been out of office. Ding said he could bear great responsibility, so the emperor summoned him, appointed him to manage the Privy Council, and ordered him to the river front to oversee the armies.

sentences.zh: 時敵兵久駐淮南，知南兵有備，漸謀北歸。

translations.literal: At that time the enemy army had long stayed in Huainan; knowing southern troops were prepared, they gradually planned to return north.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy had long remained in Huainan. Seeing that the southern armies were prepared, they gradually planned to withdraw north.

sentences.zh: 鼎曰：「金人無能為矣。

translations.literal: Ding said: "The Jin can do nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "The Jin can do nothing more."

sentences.zh: 」命諸將邀諸淮，連敗之，金人遁去。

translations.literal: " He ordered the generals to intercept them along the Huai, defeated them repeatedly, and the Jin fled away.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the generals to intercept them along the Huai, defeated them repeatedly, and the Jin withdrew.

sentences.zh: 上謂鼎曰：「近將士致勇爭先，諸路守臣亦翕然自效，乃朕用卿之力也。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Ding: "Recently soldiers have shown courage and vied to be first; prefectural defenders along every route have also willingly devoted themselves—this is the power of employing you.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said to Ding, "Lately our soldiers have fought with courage and vied to lead, and defenders along every route have rallied to serve. This is what comes of putting you to use."

sentences.zh: 」鼎謝曰：「皆出聖斷，臣何力之有焉。

translations.literal: " Ding thanked him and said: "All comes from the sacred decision—what power does this subject have?
translations.idiomatic: Ding thanked him and said, "All this comes from Your Majesty's own resolve. What strength does your servant have in it?"

sentences.zh: 」或問鼎曰：「金人傾國來攻，眾皆忷懼，公獨言不足畏，何耶？

translations.literal: " Someone asked Ding: "The Jin came with the whole nation to attack; everyone was agitated and afraid; you alone said they were not to be feared—why?
translations.idiomatic: Someone asked Ding, "The Jin came with the full power of their state and everyone was terrified. You alone said they were not to be feared—why?"

sentences.zh: 」鼎曰：「敵眾雖盛，然以豫邀而來，非其本心，戰必不力，以是知其不足畏也。

translations.literal: " Ding said: "Though the enemy's numbers are great, they came because Liu Yu invited them—not from their own heart; in battle they will surely not exert themselves; by this I know they are not to be feared.
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "Though their numbers are great, they came because Liu Yu summoned them, not from their own will. They will not fight with their full strength, and that is how I knew they were not to be feared."

sentences.zh: 」上嘗語張浚曰：「趙鼎真宰相，天使佐朕中興，可謂宗社之幸也。

translations.literal: " The emperor once said to Zhang Jun: "Zhao Ding is a true chief councillor; Heaven sent him to assist me in revival—this may be called the fortune of the altars of state.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once told Zhang Jun, "Zhao Ding is a true chief councillor. Heaven sent him to help me restore the dynasty—this is the fortune of the altars of state."

sentences.zh: 」鼎奏金人遁歸，尤當博采群言，為善後之計。

translations.literal: " Ding memorialized that with the Jin fled and gone home, it was all the more necessary to gather widely diverse opinions and plan for what comes after.
translations.idiomatic: Ding memorialized that with the Jin in retreat, the court should all the more gather wide counsel and plan for what comes next.

sentences.zh: 於是詔呂頤浩等議攻戰備禦、措置綏懷之方。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict ordered Lü Yihao and others to discuss methods of attack, defense, and arrangements for pacification and reassurance.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then ordered Lü Yihao and others to discuss methods of attack, defense, and policies for pacification.

sentences.zh: 五年，上還臨安，制以鼎守左僕射知樞密院事、張浚守右僕射兼知樞密院事，都督諸路軍馬。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the emperor returned to Lin'an; by appointment Ding was made Left Vice Director and manager of the Privy Council, Zhang Jun Right Vice Director and concurrent manager of the Privy Council, superintendent of military forces on all routes.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year the emperor returned to Lin'an. Ding was appointed Left Vice Director and manager of the Privy Council; Zhang Jun was appointed Right Vice Director and concurrent manager of the Privy Council, with command over military forces on all routes.

sentences.zh: 鼎以政事先後及人才所當召用者，條而置之座右，次第奏行之。

translations.literal: Ding listed matters of government in order of priority and men who ought to be summoned, placed them at his right hand, and presented and carried them out one by one.
translations.idiomatic: Ding listed governmental priorities and the men who ought to be appointed, kept the list at his right hand, and presented and carried out each item in turn.

sentences.zh: 制以貴州防禦使瑗為保慶軍節度使，封建國公，於行宮門外建資善堂。

translations.literal: By appointment the Defender of Guizhou Yuan was made Military Commissioner of the Baojing Army, enfeoffed as Duke of the State, and a Zishan Hall was built outside the traveling palace gate.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan, Defender of Guizhou, was appointed Military Commissioner of the Baojing Army and enfeoffed as Duke of the State, and a Hall of Worthy Learning was built outside the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 鼎薦範沖為翊善、朱震為贊讀，朝論謂二人極天下之選。

translations.literal: Ding recommended Fan Chong as attendant tutor and Zhu Zhen as attendant reader; court opinion held the two to be the finest choices under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Ding recommended Fan Chong as attendant tutor and Zhu Zhen as attendant reader. Court opinion held that no better choices could be found in the empire.

sentences.zh: 建炎初，嘗下詔以奸臣誣衊宣仁保佑之功，命史院刊修，未及行，朱勝非為相，上諭之曰：「神宗、哲宗兩朝史事多失實，非所以傳信後世，宜召範沖刊定。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyan an edict had been issued because wicked ministers slandered Empress Xuanren's protective merit, ordering the History Office to revise—before it was carried out; when Zhu Shengfei became chief councillor, the emperor instructed him: "The historical records of the Shenzong and Zhezong reigns are mostly unfaithful to fact and cannot be trusted by posterity—you should summon Fan Chong to revise and fix them.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Jianyan era an edict had been issued because wicked ministers had slandered Empress Xuanren's protective role, ordering the History Office to revise the account, but it had not yet been carried out. When Zhu Shengfei became chief councillor, the emperor instructed him, "The records of the Shenzong and Zhezong reigns often misrepresent the facts and cannot be trusted by posterity. Fan Chong should be summoned to revise them."

sentences.zh: 」勝非言：「《神宗史》增多王安石《日錄》，《哲宗史》經京、卞之手，議論多不正，命官刪修，誠足以彰二帝盛美。

translations.literal: " Shengfei said: "The History of Shenzong added much from Wang Anshi's Daily Records; the History of Zhezong passed through the hands of the Jings and Bians—the judgments are mostly incorrect; to appoint officials to delete and revise would truly suffice to display the two emperors' splendid virtue.
translations.idiomatic: Shengfei replied, "The History of Shenzong was padded with Wang Anshi's Daily Records, and the History of Zhezong was shaped by the Jing and Cai factions, with many biased judgments. Appointing officials to revise them would truly bring out the two emperors' virtues."

sentences.zh: 」會勝非去位，鼎以宰相監修二史，是非各得其正。

translations.literal: " When Shengfei left office, Ding as chief councillor supervised revision of the two histories, and right and wrong each found its proper place.
translations.idiomatic: When Shengfei left office, Ding as chief councillor supervised revision of the two histories, and truth and error were each set right.

sentences.zh: 上親書「忠正德文」四字賜鼎，又以御書《尚書》一帙賜之，曰：「《書》所載君臣相戒飭之言，所以賜卿，欲共由斯道。

translations.literal: The emperor personally wrote the four characters "Loyal, Upright, Virtuous, Cultured" and bestowed them on Ding; he also bestowed a fascicle of the imperially copied Book of Documents, saying: "The words in the Book by which ruler and minister admonish and instruct one another—I bestow this on you because I wish us to follow this way together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor personally wrote the four characters "Loyal, Upright, Virtuous, Cultured" and bestowed them on Ding. He also gave him a fascicle of the imperially copied Book of Documents, saying, "The Book records the words by which ruler and minister admonish one another. I give this to you because I wish us to walk this path together."

sentences.zh: 」鼎上疏謝。

translations.literal: " Ding submitted a memorial of thanks.
translations.idiomatic: Ding submitted a memorial of thanks.

sentences.zh: 劉豫遣子麟、猊分路入寇，時張浚屯盱眙，楊沂中屯泗，韓世忠屯楚，岳飛駐鄂，劉光世駐廬，沿江上下無兵，上與鼎以為憂。

translations.literal: Liu Yu sent his sons Lin and Ni to invade by separate routes. At that time Zhang Jun was encamped at Xuyi, Yang Yizhong at Si, Han Shizhong at Chu, Yue Fei stationed at E, Liu Guangshi at Lu—along the river above and below there were no troops; the emperor and Ding were troubled.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Yu sent his sons Lin and Ni to invade by separate routes. Zhang Jun was encamped at Xuyi, Yang Yizhong at Si, Han Shizhong at Chu, Yue Fei at Ezhou, and Liu Guangshi at Luzhou, leaving long stretches of the river undefended. The emperor and Ding were deeply concerned.

sentences.zh: 鼎移書浚，欲令俊與沂中合兵剿敵。

translations.literal: Ding sent a letter to Jun, wishing to have Jun and Yizhong combine forces to exterminate the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Ding wrote to Zhang Jun urging him to combine forces with Yang Yizhong to destroy the enemy.

sentences.zh: 光世乞舍廬還太平，又乞退保採石，鼎奏曰：「豫逆賊也，官軍與豫戰而不能勝，或更退守，何以立國？

translations.literal: Guangshi begged to abandon Lu and return to Taiping, and also begged to retreat and defend Caishi; Ding memorialized: "Yu is a rebel enemy—if the official army fights Yu and cannot win, or even retreats further to defend, how can the state stand?
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangshi asked to abandon Luzhou and return to Taiping, and then to fall back and hold Caishi. Ding memorialized, "Yu is a rebel usurper. If the imperial army cannot defeat him in battle, or retreats further to defend, how can the dynasty stand?"

sentences.zh: 今賊已渡淮，當亟遣張俊合光世之軍盡掃淮南之寇，然後議去留。

translations.literal: Now the bandits have already crossed the Huai—we should urgently send Zhang Jun to combine with Guangshi's army and thoroughly sweep away the Huainan raiders, and only then discuss staying or leaving.
translations.idiomatic: The enemy has already crossed the Huai. Zhang Jun should be sent at once to join Liu Guangshi and sweep the Huainan raiders clean, and only then should we discuss withdrawal."

sentences.zh: 」上善其策，詔二將進兵。

translations.literal: " The emperor approved his plan and ordered the two generals to advance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved his plan and ordered the two generals to advance.

sentences.zh: 俊軍至藕塘與猊戰，大破之。

translations.literal: Jun's army reached Outang and fought Ni, routing him greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun's army reached Outang, fought Ni, and routed him.

sentences.zh: 鼎命沂中趨合肥以會光世，光世已棄廬回江北。

translations.literal: Ding ordered Yizhong to hurry to Hefei to join Guangshi; Guangshi had already abandoned Lu and returned north of the river.
translations.idiomatic: Ding ordered Yang Yizhong to hurry to Hefei to join Liu Guangshi, but Guangshi had already abandoned Luzhou and withdrawn north of the river.

sentences.zh: 浚以書告鼎，鼎白上詔浚：有不用命者，聽以軍法從事。

translations.literal: Jun reported by letter to Ding; Ding informed the emperor, who edicted Jun: where anyone disobeys orders, he may deal with them according to military law.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun reported this to Ding in a letter. Ding informed the emperor, who issued an edict to Jun: whoever disobeyed orders might be dealt with under military law.

sentences.zh: 光世大駭，復進至肥河與麟戰，破之。

translations.literal: Guangshi was greatly alarmed, advanced again to Fei River and fought Lin, and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Greatly alarmed, Liu Guangshi advanced again to the Fei River, fought Lin, and defeated him.

sentences.zh: 麟、猊拔柵遁去。

translations.literal: Lin and Ni pulled up their palisades and fled away.
translations.idiomatic: Lin and Ni broke camp and fled.

sentences.zh: 浚在江上，嘗遣其屬呂祉入奏事，所言誇大，鼎每抑之。

translations.literal: Jun was on the river front and once sent his subordinate Lü Zhi to enter court and report; what he said was exaggerated, and Ding always restrained it.
translations.idiomatic: While on the river front, Zhang Jun sent his subordinate Lü Zhi to court to report. Lü's reports were inflated, and Ding always reined them in.

sentences.zh: 上謂鼎曰：「他日張浚與卿不和，必呂祉也。

translations.literal: The emperor said to Ding: "If one day Zhang Jun and you are not in harmony, it will surely be because of Lü Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor told Ding, "If you and Zhang Jun ever fall out, Lü Zhi will be the cause."

sentences.zh: 」後浚因論事，語意微侵鼎，鼎言：「臣初與浚如兄弟，因呂祉離間，遂爾睽異。

translations.literal: " Later Jun, while discussing affairs, let his words slightly encroach on Ding; Ding said: "At first Jun and I were like brothers; because Lü Zhi drove us apart, we came to this estrangement.
translations.idiomatic: Later, in a discussion of policy, Zhang Jun's words carried a slight sting toward Ding. Ding said, "Jun and I were once like brothers. Lü Zhi drove us apart, and that is how we came to this breach."

sentences.zh: 今浚成功，當使展盡底蘊，浚當留，臣當去。

translations.literal: Now that Jun has achieved success, he should be allowed to bring out all his depth; Jun should stay, and I should go.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Jun has succeeded, he should be allowed to deploy all his talents. He should stay, and I should go."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「俟浚歸議之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Wait until Jun returns and we shall discuss it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Wait until Jun returns and we shall discuss it."

sentences.zh: 」浚嘗奏乞幸建康，而鼎與折彥質請回蹕臨安。

translations.literal: " Jun once memorialized asking that the emperor visit Jiankang, while Ding and Zhe Yanzhi asked that the imperial carriage return to Lin'an.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun memorialized asking the emperor to move to Jiankang, while Ding and Zhe Yanzhi asked that the court return to Lin'an.

sentences.zh: 暨浚還，乞乘勝攻河南，且罷劉光世軍政。

translations.literal: When Jun returned, he asked to follow victory and attack Henan, and also to dismiss Liu Guangshi from military command.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun returned, he asked to press the advantage and attack Henan, and also to strip Liu Guangshi of military command.

sentences.zh: 鼎言：「擒豫固易耳，然得河南，能保金人不內侵乎？

translations.literal: Ding said: "Capturing Yu would indeed be easy—but if we gain Henan, can we guarantee the Jin will not invade inward?
translations.idiomatic: Ding objected, "Capturing Yu would indeed be easy, but even if we took Henan, could we keep the Jin from invading again?"

sentences.zh: 光世累世為將，無故而罷之，恐人心不安。

translations.literal: Guangshi has been a general for generations; to dismiss him without cause would, I fear, unsettle men's hearts.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Guangshi comes from a line of generals. To dismiss him without cause would unsettle men's hearts."

sentences.zh: 」浚滋不悅。

translations.literal: " Jun grew ever displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun grew ever more displeased.

sentences.zh: 鼎以觀文殿大學士知紹興府。

translations.literal: Ding was made Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture and prefect of Shaoxing.
translations.idiomatic: Ding was appointed Grand Academician of the Hall for Viewing Culture and prefect of Shaoxing.

sentences.zh: 七年，上幸建康，罷劉光世，以王德為都統制，酈瓊副之，並聽參謀、兵部尚書呂祉節度制。

translations.literal: In the seventh year the emperor visited Jiankang, dismissed Liu Guangshi, made Wang De overall commander with Li Qiong as his deputy, both subject to the planning control of Counsellor and Minister of War Lü Zhi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year the emperor visited Jiankang, dismissed Liu Guangshi, appointed Wang De overall commander with Li Qiong as deputy, both under the command of Counsellor and Minister of War Lü Zhi.

sentences.zh: 瓊與德有宿怨，訴於祉，不得直，執祉以全軍降偽齊。

translations.literal: Qiong and De had an old grudge; Qiong appealed to Zhi but got no justice; he seized Zhi and led the whole army to surrender to the puppet Qi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Qiong and Wang De had an old grievance. Li Qiong appealed to Lü Zhi but got no justice, seized him, and led the entire army in surrender to the puppet Qi regime.

sentences.zh: 浚引咎去位，乃以萬壽觀使兼侍讀召鼎，入對，拜尚書左僕射、同中書門下平章事兼樞密使，進四官。

translations.literal: Jun took blame and left office; then Ding was summoned as Commissioner of the Wanshou Abbey and concurrent palace reader; entering audience he was appointed Left Vice Director of the Department of State Affairs, Concurrent Master of the Hall with Assent at the Secretariat-Chancellery Gate, and concurrent Privy Councillor—promoted four ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jun took the blame and resigned. Ding was summoned as Commissioner of the Wanshou Abbey and concurrent palace reader. At audience he was appointed Left Vice Director, Concurrent Master of the Hall with Assent, and concurrent Privy Councillor—a promotion of four ranks.

sentences.zh: 上言：「淮西之報初至，執政奏事皆失措，惟朕不為動。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "When the first report from Huai West arrived, the chief administrators presenting affairs were all at a loss—only I was unmoved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "When the first report from Huai West arrived, the chief administrators were all at a loss in presenting affairs—only I was unmoved."

sentences.zh: 」鼎曰：「今見諸將，尤須靜以待之，不然益增其驕蹇之心。

translations.literal: " Ding said: "When you now see the generals, you must above all meet them with calm—otherwise you will only increase their arrogance and insolence.
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "When you meet the generals now, you must above all receive them calmly. Otherwise you will only feed their arrogance."

sentences.zh: 」台諫交論淮西無備，鼎曰：「行朝擁兵十萬，敵騎直來，自足抗之，設有他虞，鼎身任其責。

translations.literal: " Censors and remonstrators repeatedly debated that Huai West was unprepared; Ding said: "The traveling court holds a hundred thousand troops—if enemy cavalry come straight on, that is enough to resist them; if there be other worry, Ding personally bears the responsibility.
translations.idiomatic: Censors and remonstrators repeatedly argued that Huai West was undefended. Ding said, "The traveling court has a hundred thousand troops. If enemy cavalry come straight at us, that is enough to resist them. If anything else goes wrong, I will take personal responsibility."

sentences.zh: 」淮西迄無驚。

translations.literal: " Huai West in the end had no alarm.
translations.idiomatic: In the end Huai West saw no disturbance.

sentences.zh: 鼎嘗乞降詔安撫淮西，上曰：「俟行遣張浚，朕當下罪己之詔。

translations.literal: Ding once asked that an edict be issued to pacify Huai West; the emperor said: "Wait until Zhang Jun is dispatched on assignment—I shall then issue a self-reproach edict.
translations.idiomatic: Ding once asked that an edict be issued to reassure Huai West. The emperor said, "Wait until Zhang Jun is dispatched on assignment. I shall then issue an edict of self-reproach."

sentences.zh: 」鼎言：「浚已落職。

translations.literal: " Ding said: "Jun has already been dismissed from office.
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "Jun has already been dismissed from office."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「浚罪當遠竄。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Jun's crime deserves exile to a distant place.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Jun's crime deserves exile to a distant place."

sentences.zh: 」鼎奏：「浚母老，且有勤王功。

translations.literal: " Ding memorialized: "Jun's mother is old, and he also has the merit of rushing to the emperor's aid.
translations.idiomatic: Ding memorialized, "Jun's mother is elderly, and he also has the merit of rushing to the emperor's aid."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「功過自不相掩。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Merit and fault do not cancel each other.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Merit and fault do not cancel each other."

sentences.zh: 」已而內批出，浚謫置嶺南，鼎留不下。

translations.literal: " Before long an inner draft issued exiling Jun to Lingnan; Ding withheld it and did not promulgate it.
translations.idiomatic: Before long an inner draft issued, banishing Jun to Lingnan. Ding withheld it and did not promulgate it.

sentences.zh: 詰旦，經同列救解，上怒殊未釋，鼎力懇曰：「浚罪不過片策耳。

translations.literal: At dawn, after passing through colleagues who sought to save and explain, the emperor's anger was still far from eased; Ding pleaded earnestly: "Jun's fault is no more than a single flawed plan.
translations.idiomatic: At dawn, after his colleagues interceded, the emperor's anger had barely eased. Ding pleaded earnestly, "Jun's fault amounts to no more than a single flawed plan."

sentences.zh: 凡人計慮，豈不欲萬全，儻因一失，便置之死地，後有奇謀秘計，誰復敢言者。

translations.literal: When any man calculates and considers, does he not wish complete safety? If for one failure he is placed in a living death, who afterward will dare speak bold plans and secret stratagems?
translations.idiomatic: Any man who plans wishes above all to be safe. If one mistake sends him to his ruin, who will dare offer bold plans afterward?"

sentences.zh: 此事自關朝廷，非獨私浚也。

translations.literal: This matter concerns the court itself—it is not merely for Jun's private sake.
translations.idiomatic: This concerns the court itself, not Jun alone."

sentences.zh: 」上意乃解，遂以散官分司，居永州。

translations.literal: " The emperor's mind was then eased; Jun was made a standalone official without portfolio and sent to live in Yongzhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor relented. Jun was made a standalone official without portfolio and sent to live in Yongzhou.

sentences.zh: 鼎既再相，或議其無所施設，鼎聞之曰：「今日之事如人患羸，當靜以養之。

translations.literal: Now that Ding was chief councillor again, some criticized him for accomplishing nothing; when Ding heard it he said: "Today's affairs are like a man weakened by illness—one should nurture him with calm.
translations.idiomatic: After Ding became chief councillor again, some criticized him for doing too little. When he heard this he said, "The state today is like a man weakened by illness. It must be nursed in quiet."

sentences.zh: 若復加攻砭，必傷元氣矣。

translations.literal: If we again apply aggressive acupuncture, we will surely harm the vital energy.
translations.idiomatic: If we apply harsh remedies again, we will damage its vital strength."

sentences.zh: 」金人廢劉豫，鼎遣間招河南守將，壽、亳、陳、蔡之間，往往舉城或率部曲來歸，得精兵萬余，馬數千。

translations.literal: " The Jin deposed Liu Yu; Ding sent agents to recruit commanders defending Henan; between Shou, Bo, Chen, and Cai, cities often rose or led their bands to submit, gaining more than ten thousand elite troops and several thousand horses.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin deposed Liu Yu. Ding sent agents to win over Henan commanders. Between Shou, Bo, Chen, and Cai, cities often surrendered or garrison commanders came over with their troops, yielding more than ten thousand elite soldiers and several thousand horses.

sentences.zh: 知廬州劉錡亦奏言：「淮北歸正者不絕，度今歲可得四五萬。

translations.literal: Prefect of Luzhou Liu Qi also memorialized: "Defectors from north of the Huai come without stop—I estimate this year we may gain forty or fifty thousand.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect of Luzhou, Liu Qi, also memorialized, "Defectors from north of the Huai keep coming. I estimate we may gain forty or fifty thousand this year."

sentences.zh: 」上喜曰：「朕常慮江、池數百里備禦空虛，今得此軍可無患矣。」

translations.literal: " The emperor said joyfully: "I have always worried that for several hundred li along the river and Chizhou defenses were empty—now with this army we may be free of worry."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said with pleasure, "I have long worried that defenses were empty for hundreds of li along the river and Chizhou. With this army we need fear no more."

sentences.zh: 金人遣使議和，朝論以為不可信，上怒。

translations.literal: The Jin sent envoys to discuss peace; court opinion held it untrustworthy; the emperor was angry.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin sent envoys to discuss peace. Court opinion held them untrustworthy, and the emperor was angry.

sentences.zh: 鼎曰：「陛下于金人有不共戴天之讎，今屈己請和，不憚為之者，以梓宮及母后耳。

translations.literal: Ding said: "Your Majesty bears with the Jin a hatred that cannot share the same sky under one canopy; that you now humble yourself to seek peace, unafraid to do so, is only for the imperial coffin and the empress dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "Your Majesty bears with the Jin a hatred that cannot be shared under the same heaven. That you now humble yourself to seek peace—you do so only for the imperial coffin and the empress dowager."

sentences.zh: 群臣憤懣之辭，出於愛君，不可以為罪。

translations.literal: The angry and indignant words of officials and ministers come from love of the ruler—they cannot be treated as crime.
translations.idiomatic: The angry words of your ministers come from love of their ruler. They cannot be treated as offenses."

sentences.zh: 陛下宜諭之曰：'講和非吾意，以親故，不得已為之。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should instruct them: 'Seeking peace is not my wish; for the sake of kin, I cannot but do it.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should tell them, 'Peace is not my wish. For the sake of my kin I cannot but seek it.

sentences.zh: 但得梓宮及母后還，敵雖渝盟，吾無憾焉。

translations.literal: If only the imperial coffin and the empress dowager return, though the enemy break the covenant, I shall have no regret.
translations.idiomatic: Once the imperial coffin and the empress dowager are returned, even if the enemy break the treaty, I shall have no regret.

sentences.zh: '」上從其言，群議遂息。

translations.literal: '" The emperor followed his words and public debate then ceased.
translations.idiomatic: '" The emperor followed his advice, and the uproar subsided.

sentences.zh: 潘良貴以向子諲奏事久，叱之退。

translations.literal: Pan Lianggui, because Xiang Ziyin reported affairs at length, rebuked him and sent him away.
translations.idiomatic: Pan Lianggui, because Xiang Ziyin took too long in presenting affairs, rebuked him and sent him away.

sentences.zh: 上欲抵良貴罪，常同為之辨，欲並逐同。

translations.literal: The emperor wished to charge Lianggui with an offense; Chang Tong spoke in his defense and wished to have Tong expelled as well.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor wished to punish Lianggui. Chang Tong defended him, and the emperor wished to expel Chang Tong as well.

sentences.zh: 鼎奏：「子諲雖無罪，而同與良貴不宜逐。

translations.literal: Ding memorialized: "Though Ziyin is without fault, Tong and Lianggui ought not be expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Ding memorialized, "Ziyin may be without fault, but Tong and Lianggui ought not be expelled."

sentences.zh: 」二人竟出。

translations.literal: " In the end both men were dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: In the end both men were dismissed from office.

sentences.zh: 給事中張致遠謂不應以一子諲出二佳士，不書黃，上怒，顧鼎曰：「固知致遠必繳駁。

translations.literal: Supervising Secretariat drafter Zhang Zhiyuan said one Ziyin should not cause two excellent men to be dismissed; he refused to write the yellow draft; the emperor was angry and turned to Ding: "I knew Zhiyuan would certainly return the draft for revision.
translations.idiomatic: Supervising Secretariat drafter Zhang Zhiyuan argued that Xiang Ziyin alone should not cost two excellent men their posts and refused to endorse the edict. The emperor was angry and said to Ding, "I knew Zhiyuan would block this."

sentences.zh: 」鼎問：「何也？

translations.literal: " Ding asked: "Why?
translations.idiomatic: Ding asked, "Why?"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「與諸人善。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "He is on good terms with those men.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "He is on good terms with those men."

sentences.zh: 」蓋已有先入之言，由是不樂於鼎矣。

translations.literal: " There had already been preconceived words—henceforth the emperor was displeased with Ding.
translations.idiomatic: There had already been preconceived words against Ding, and from this the emperor grew displeased with him.

sentences.zh: 秦檜繼留身奏事，既出，鼎問：「帝何言？

translations.literal: Qin Hui then stayed behind to report; when he came out, Ding asked: "What did the emperor say?
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui then stayed behind to report to the emperor. When he came out, Ding asked, "What did the emperor say?"

sentences.zh: 」檜曰：「上無他，恐丞相不樂耳。

translations.literal: " Hui said: "The emperor had nothing else—he only feared the chief councillor would be displeased.
translations.idiomatic: Hui said, "Nothing else. He only feared the chief councillor would be displeased."

sentences.zh: 」御筆和州防禦使璩除節鉞，封國公。

translations.literal: " By imperial brush the Defender of Hezhou Qu was appointed to military command and enfeoffed as Duke of the State.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial brush Qu, Defender of Hezhou, was given a military commission and enfeoffed as Duke of the State.

sentences.zh: 鼎奏：「建國雖未正名，天下皆知陛下有子，社謖大計也。

translations.literal: Ding memorialized: "Though enfeoffment as Duke of the State is not yet formalized by name, all under Heaven know Your Majesty has a son—it is a great plan for the altars of soil and grain.
translations.idiomatic: Ding memorialized, "Though the heir has not yet been formally named, all under Heaven know Your Majesty has a son. This is a matter of state on which the dynasty's fate depends."

sentences.zh: 在今禮數不得不異，所以系人心不使之二三而惑也。

translations.literal: For now ritual and ceremony cannot but differ—this is to bind men's hearts and keep them from wavering in doubt.
translations.idiomatic: For now the rites must distinguish him clearly, so as to fix men's hearts and keep them from wavering in doubt."

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「姑徐之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "For now let it wait.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "For now let it wait."

sentences.zh: 」檜後留身，不知所云。

translations.literal: " Hui later stayed behind again; no one knows what he said.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui stayed behind again afterward. No one knows what he said.

sentences.zh: 鼎嘗辟和議，與檜意不合，及鼎以爭璩封國事拂上意，檜乘間擠鼎，又薦蕭振為侍御史。

translations.literal: Ding had once opposed the peace talks; his views did not agree with Hui's. When Ding, by disputing Qu's enfeoffment as Duke of the State, went against the emperor's wishes, Hui seized the opportunity to squeeze Ding out, and further recommended Xiao Zhen as Attending Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Ding had opposed the peace talks, and his views clashed with Qin Hui's. When Ding provoked the emperor's displeasure by disputing the enfeoffment of Qu as heir, Hui seized the opening to force him out and recommended Xiao Zhen as Attending Censor.

sentences.zh: 振本鼎所引，及入台，劾參知政事劉大中罷之。

translations.literal: Zhen had originally been brought in by Ding; once he entered the Censorate, he impeached Vice Grand Councillor Liu Dazhong and had him dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen had originally been Ding's appointee. Once he entered the Censorate, he impeached Vice Grand Councillor Liu Dazhong and had him removed from office.

sentences.zh: 鼎曰：「振意不在大中也。

translations.literal: Ding said: "Zhen's intent is not directed at Dazhong.
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "Zhen's target is not Dazhong at all.

sentences.zh: 」振亦謂人曰：「趙丞相不待論，當自為去就。

translations.literal: " Zhen also said to others: "Chief Councillor Zhao needs no discussion—he should decide for himself whether to stay or go.
translations.idiomatic: Zhen also told others, "Chief Councillor Zhao needs no argument. He should decide for himself whether to stay or go.

sentences.zh: 」會殿中侍御史張戒論給事中勾濤，濤言：「戒之擊臣，乃趙鼎意。

translations.literal: " At that time Palace Attending Censor Zhang Jie criticized Supervising Secretary Gou Tao; Tao said: "Jie's attack on me is Zhao Ding's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward, Palace Attending Censor Zhang Jie criticized Supervising Secretary Gou Tao. Tao said, "Jie's attack on me comes from Zhao Ding.

sentences.zh: 」因詆鼎結台諫及諸將。

translations.literal: " Thereupon he slandered Ding for colluding with censors, remonstrators, and various generals.
translations.idiomatic: He then accused Ding of colluding with censors, remonstrators, and military commanders.

sentences.zh: 上聞益疑，鼎引疾求免，言：「大中持正論，為章惇、蔡京之黨所嫉。

translations.literal: When the emperor heard this he grew yet more suspicious. Ding pleaded illness and asked to be dismissed, saying: "Dazhong held to upright views and was envied by the faction of Zhang Dun and Cai Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor heard this, his suspicions deepened. Ding pleaded illness and asked to resign, saying, "Dazhong held to upright views and was hated by the Zhang Dun and Cai Jing faction.

sentences.zh: 臣議論出處與大中同，大中去，臣何可留？

translations.literal: My views on entering and leaving office are the same as Dazhong's; if Dazhong goes, how can I remain?
translations.idiomatic: My principles of public service match Dazhong's. If he goes, how can I stay?

sentences.zh: 」乃以忠武節度使出知紹興府，尋加檢校少傅，改奉國軍節度使。

translations.literal: " He was then sent out as Military Commissioner of Zhongwu to serve as prefect of Shaoxing; soon he was given the additional title Honorary Junior Tutor and transferred to Military Commissioner of Fengguo.
translations.idiomatic: He was sent out as Military Commissioner of Zhongwu to govern Shaoxing prefecture. Soon he was given the additional title Honorary Junior Tutor and transferred to Military Commissioner of Fengguo.

sentences.zh: 檜率執政往餞其行，鼎不為禮，一揖而去，檜益憾之。

translations.literal: Hui led the chief administrators to see him off on his departure; Ding showed him no courtesy—bowed once and left; Hui resented him all the more.
translations.idiomatic: Qin Hui led the chief administrators to see him off. Ding offered no courtesy, gave a single bow, and departed. Hui resented him all the more.

sentences.zh: 鼎既去，王庶入對，上謂庶曰：「趙鼎兩為相，于國有大功，再贊親征皆能決勝，又鎮撫建康，回鑾無患，他人所不及也。

translations.literal: After Ding had gone, Wang Shu entered audience; the emperor said to Shu: "Zhao Ding served twice as chief councillor; he rendered great service to the state. Both times he assisted the emperor on campaign he could secure victory; he also pacified and settled Jiankang, so the return of the imperial carriage was without worry—what others could not match.
translations.idiomatic: After Ding had left, Wang Shu had audience with the emperor, who said to him, "Zhao Ding served twice as chief councillor and rendered the state great service. Both times he assisted the emperor on campaign, he helped secure victory. He also pacified Jiankang, so the return of the court was uneventful. No one else could match that.

sentences.zh: 」先是，王倫使金，從鼎受使指。

translations.literal: " Earlier, Wang Lun was sent as envoy to the Jin and received his mission instructions from Ding.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when Wang Lun was sent as envoy to the Jin, he received his instructions from Ding.

sentences.zh: 問禮數，則答以君臣之分已定；

translations.literal: When asked about ritual and ceremony, he answered that the distinction between sovereign and subject was already fixed;
translations.idiomatic: When asked about ritual protocol, Ding answered that the distinction between sovereign and subject was already settled;

sentences.zh: 問地界，則答以大河為界。

translations.literal: when asked about territorial boundaries, he answered that the Great River should be the border.
translations.idiomatic: when asked about territorial boundaries, he answered that the Yellow River should serve as the border.

sentences.zh: 二者從事之大者，或不從則已。

translations.literal: These two were the greater matters in conducting affairs; if they were not accepted, so be it.
translations.idiomatic: These were the two chief points of the mission. If the Jin would not accept them, the talks should end.

sentences.zh: 倫受命而行。

translations.literal: Lun received the commission and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Lun received his instructions and set out.

sentences.zh: 至是，倫與金使俱來，以撫諭江南為名，上歎息謂庶曰：「使五日前得此報，趙鼎豈可去耶？」

translations.literal: At this time Lun came together with the Jin envoy, under the name of reassuring Jiangnan; the emperor sighed and said to Shu: "If we had received this report five days earlier, how could Zhao Ding have been allowed to go?"
translations.idiomatic: By then Lun had returned with a Jin envoy, nominally to reassure Jiangnan. The emperor sighed and said to Shu, "If we had had this report five days ago, how could Zhao Ding have been allowed to leave?"

sentences.zh: 初，車駕還臨安，內侍移竹栽入內，鼎見，責之曰：「艮岳花石之擾，皆出汝曹，今欲蹈前轍耶？

translations.literal: Earlier, when the imperial carriage returned to Lin'an, a palace eunuch moved bamboo plantings into the inner palace; when Ding saw it he rebuked him, saying: "The Genyue Flower-and-Stone affliction all came from you lot—do you now wish to follow the old rut?
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, when the court returned to Lin'an, a palace eunuch was transplanting bamboo into the inner palace. When Ding saw this he rebuked him, saying, "The Genyue Flower-and-Stone extravagance all came from men like you. Do you now wish to repeat that ruin?

sentences.zh: 」因奏其事，上改容謝之。

translations.literal: " He then memorialized on the matter; the emperor changed expression and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized on the matter, and the emperor changed expression and apologized.

sentences.zh: 有戶部官進錢入宮者，鼎召至相府切責之。

translations.literal: There was a Revenue Department official who presented money into the palace; Ding summoned him to the chief councillor's office and sternly rebuked him.
translations.idiomatic: When a Revenue Department official presented money to the palace, Ding summoned him to the chief councillor's office and sternly rebuked him.

sentences.zh: 翌日，問上曰：「某人獻錢耶？

translations.literal: The next day he asked the emperor: "Did a certain person present money?
translations.idiomatic: The next day he asked the emperor, "Did so-and-so present money?

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「朕求之也。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "I sought it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "I asked for it.

sentences.zh: 」鼎奏：「某人不當獻，陛下不當求。

translations.literal: " Ding memorialized: "That person ought not to have presented it; Your Majesty ought not to have sought it.
translations.idiomatic: Ding memorialized, "That man should not have offered it, and Your Majesty should not have asked for it.

sentences.zh: 」遂出其人與郡。

translations.literal: " Thereupon that person was sent out to a prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The man was then dismissed to a prefectural post.

sentences.zh: 鼎嘗薦胡寅、魏矼、晏敦復、潘良貴、呂本中、張致遠等數十人分佈朝列。

translations.literal: Ding once recommended Hu Yin, Wei Gang, Yan Dunfu, Pan Lianggui, Lü Benzhong, Zhang Zhiyuan, and several dozen others, distributing them through the court ranks.
translations.idiomatic: Ding had once recommended Hu Yin, Wei Gang, Yan Dunfu, Pan Lianggui, Lü Benzhong, Zhang Zhiyuan, and dozens of others, placing them throughout the court.

sentences.zh: 暨再相，奏曰：「今清議所與，如劉大中、胡寅、呂本中、常同、林季仲之流，陛下能用之乎？

translations.literal: When he became chief councillor again, he memorialized, saying: "Those whom clear-minded opinion favors, such as Liu Dazhong, Hu Yin, Lü Benzhong, Chang Tong, Lin Jizhong, and the like—can Your Majesty employ them?
translations.idiomatic: When he became chief councillor again, he memorialized, "Men of clear opinion favor such figures as Liu Dazhong, Hu Yin, Lü Benzhong, Chang Tong, and Lin Jizhong. Can Your Majesty employ them?

sentences.zh: 妒賢長惡，如趙霈、胡世將、周秘、陳公輔之徒，陛下能去之乎？

translations.literal: Those who envy the worthy and nurture evil, such as Zhao Pei, Hu Shijiang, Zhou Mi, Chen Gongfu, and the like—can Your Majesty remove them?
translations.idiomatic: Men who envy talent and abet wickedness, such as Zhao Pei, Hu Shijiang, Zhou Mi, and Chen Gongfu—can Your Majesty remove them?

sentences.zh: 」上為徙世將，而公輔等尋補外。

translations.literal: " The emperor accordingly transferred Shijiang; Gongfu and the others were soon sent out to provincial posts.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor transferred Shijiang, and Gongfu and the others were soon sent out to provincial posts.

sentences.zh: 上嘗中批二人付廟堂升擢。

translations.literal: The emperor once by inner draft handed two men to the chief ministers for promotion.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once issued an inner draft ordering the chief ministers to promote two men.

sentences.zh: 鼎奏：「疏遠小臣，陛下何由得其姓名？

translations.literal: Ding memorialized: "Obscure petty officials—how would Your Majesty come by their names?
translations.idiomatic: Ding memorialized, "These are obscure minor officials. How would Your Majesty even know their names?

sentences.zh: 」上謂：「常同實稱之。

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "Chang Tong truly praised them.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said, "Chang Tong did recommend them.

sentences.zh: 」鼎曰：「同知其賢，何不露章薦引？」

translations.literal: " Ding said: "If Tong knew them to be worthy, why did he not submit an open memorial recommending them?"
translations.idiomatic: Ding said, "If Tong knew them to be worthy, why did he not submit an open memorial recommending them?"

sentences.zh: 始，浚薦秦檜可與共大事，鼎再相亦以為言。

translations.literal: At the beginning, Jun recommended that Qin Hui could be joined in great affairs; when Ding became chief councillor again he said the same.
translations.idiomatic: At first Zhang Jun had recommended Qin Hui as a man with whom great affairs could be shared, and when Ding became chief councillor again he said the same.

sentences.zh: 然檜機阱深險，外和而中異。

translations.literal: Yet Hui's snares were deep and treacherous; outwardly conciliatory but inwardly at odds.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Hui was deep and treacherous in his intrigues—conciliatory in manner but at odds at heart.

sentences.zh: 浚初求去，有旨召鼎。

translations.literal: When Jun first asked to leave, an imperial order summoned Ding.
translations.idiomatic: When Jun first asked to resign, an imperial order summoned Ding back.

sentences.zh: 鼎至越丐祠，檜惡其逼己，徙知泉州，又諷謝祖信論鼎嘗受張邦昌偽命，遂奪節。

translations.literal: When Ding reached Yue and asked for a sinecure post, Hui hated his pressure on himself; he was transferred to govern Quanzhou; Hui also prompted Xie Zuxin to charge that Ding had once accepted a commission from the puppet Zhang Bangchang, and his military commission was then stripped.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding reached Yue and asked for a sinecure, Hui resented his pressure and had him transferred to Quanzhou. Hui also prompted Xie Zuxin to charge that Ding had once accepted an appointment from the puppet Zhang Bangchang, and Ding's military commission was stripped.

sentences.zh: 御史中丞王次翁論鼎治郡廢馳，命提舉洞霄宮。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Wang Cien charged that Ding in governing his prefecture had neglected his duties; he was ordered to serve as Commissioner of the Dongxiao Abbey.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Wang Cien charged that Ding had neglected his duties as prefect, and he was appointed Commissioner of the Dongxiao Abbey.

sentences.zh: 鼎自泉州歸，復上書言時政，檜忌其復用，諷次翁又論其嘗受偽命，乾沒都督府錢十七萬緡，謫官居興化軍。

translations.literal: When Ding returned from Quanzhou he again submitted a memorial on current affairs; Hui, fearing his return to office, prompted Cien again to charge that he had once accepted a puppet commission and had embezzled one hundred seventy thousand strings of cash from the chief commander's office; he was demoted and sent to live in Xinghua Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Ding returned from Quanzhou he memorialized again on current affairs. Hui, fearing his return to office, prompted Cien to charge again that he had accepted a puppet appointment and embezzled one hundred seventy thousand strings of cash from the chief commander's office. He was demoted and sent to live in Xinghua Army.

sentences.zh: 論者猶不已，移漳州，又責清遠軍節度副使，潮州安置。

translations.literal: The critics still did not cease; he was moved to Zhangzhou, then punished as Vice Military Commissioner of Qingyuan Army and placed under residence restriction in Chaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: His critics were still not satisfied. He was moved to Zhangzhou, then reduced to Vice Military Commissioner of Qingyuan Army and placed under residence restriction in Chaozhou.

sentences.zh: 在潮五年，杜門謝客，時事不掛口，有問者，但引咎而已。

translations.literal: During five years in Chaozhou he shut his door and declined visitors; current affairs never crossed his lips; if asked, he only took blame upon himself.
translations.idiomatic: For five years in Chaozhou he shut his doors to visitors and never spoke of current affairs. If asked, he took blame upon himself and nothing more.

sentences.zh: 中丞詹大方誣其受賄，屬潮守放編置人移吉陽軍，鼎謝表曰：「白首何歸，悵餘生之無幾，丹心未泯，誓九死以不移。

translations.literal: Censor-in-Chief Zhan Dafang falsely charged him with accepting bribes and instructed the prefect of Chaozhou to banish him under restricted residence to Jiyang Army; Ding's memorial of thanks said: "With white hair, whither shall I return? I grieve that little life remains; my loyal heart is not yet extinguished—I vow that though I die nine times I shall not change.
translations.idiomatic: Censor-in-Chief Zhan Dafang falsely charged him with accepting bribes and had the prefect of Chaozhou banish him under restricted residence to Jiyang Army. In his memorial of thanks Ding wrote, "White-haired, where may I return? I grieve that little life remains. My loyal heart is not yet extinguished. Though I die nine times, I shall not waver.

sentences.zh: 」檜見之曰：「此老倔強猶昔。」

translations.literal: " When Hui saw it he said: "This old man is obstinate as ever."
translations.idiomatic: When Hui saw it he said, "This old man is as stubborn as ever."

sentences.zh: 鼎為文渾然天成，凡高宗處分軍國機事，多其視草，有擬奏表疏、雜詩文二百餘篇，號《得全集》，行於世。

translations.literal: Ding's writing was natural and complete as if made by Heaven; of Gaozong's disposition of military and state secrets, much was drafted at his hand; there were more than two hundred memorials, petitions, mixed poems and prose, titled Complete Collection of De, circulating in the world.
translations.idiomatic: Ding's prose flowed with natural grace. Most of Gaozong's dispatches on military and state affairs passed through his hand. More than two hundred memorials, petitions, poems, and essays survive, collected as the Complete Collection of De and circulated widely.

sentences.zh: 論中興賢相，以鼎為稱首雲。

translations.literal: In discussing worthy chief ministers of the Restoration, Ding is named first, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: Among the worthy chief ministers of the Restoration, Ding is ranked first.

sentences.zh: 論曰：夫謀國用兵之道，有及時乘銳而可以立功者，有養威持重而後能有為者，二者之設施不同，其為忠一而已。

translations.literal: Commentary says: In the way of planning for the state and employing troops, there are those who seize the moment and ride sharp momentum to achieve merit, and those who nurture prestige and hold weight before they can accomplish anything—the two differ in application, yet their loyalty is one.
translations.idiomatic: Commentary: In planning for the state and deploying troops, some men achieve merit by seizing the moment and pressing an advantage, while others must nurture strength and bide their time before they can act. The methods differ, but loyalty is the same.

sentences.zh: 方金人逼二帝北行，宗社失主，宗澤一呼，而河北義旅數十萬眾若響之赴聲，實由澤之忠忱義氣有以風動之，抑斯民目睹君父之陷於塗淖，孰無憤激之心哉。

translations.literal: Just as the Jin forced the two emperors northward and the altars of state lost their lord, Zong Ze gave one call and several hundred thousand righteous bands of Hebei responded as echo to sound—truly because Ze's loyal devotion and righteous spirit moved them by example; yet did not this people, seeing their sovereign and father sink into mire, each lack a heart of indignant zeal?
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin drove the two emperors north and the dynasty lost its sovereign, Zong Ze gave a single call and several hundred thousand volunteer armies in Hebei rallied as if echoing his voice. This was truly because Ze's loyal devotion and righteous spirit moved them—but who among the people, seeing sovereign and father sink into ruin, would not burn with indignation?

sentences.zh: 使當其時澤得勇往直前，無或齟齬牽制之，則反二帝，復舊都，特一指顧間耳。

translations.literal: If at that time Ze had been allowed to press forward without contradiction or restraint, then recovering the two emperors and restoring the old capital would have been but a turn of the hand and a glance.
translations.idiomatic: If Ze had been allowed to press forward at that time without obstruction or restraint, recovering the two emperors and retaking the old capital would have been the work of a moment.

sentences.zh: 黃潛善、汪伯彥嫉能而惎功，使澤不得信其志，發憤而薨，豈不悲哉！

translations.literal: Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan envied ability and begrudged achievement, so that Ze could not fulfill his will; he died in impassioned grief—how is it not lamentable!
translations.idiomatic: Huang Qianshan and Wang Boyan envied talent and begrudged success, so Ze could never fulfill his purpose. He died in impassioned grief. How lamentable!

sentences.zh: 及趙鼎為相，則南北之勢成矣。

translations.literal: By the time Zhao Ding became chief councillor, the north-south configuration of power was already set.
translations.idiomatic: By the time Zhao Ding became chief councillor, the north-south balance of power was already set.

sentences.zh: 兩敵之相持，非有灼然可乘之釁，則養吾力以俟時，否則，徒取危困之辱。

translations.literal: When two enemies stand in stalemate, unless there is a clear and exploitable breach, one should nurture one's strength and await the time—otherwise one only invites the disgrace of peril and distress.
translations.idiomatic: When two enemies stand locked in stalemate, unless a clear opening appears, one must conserve strength and wait for the right moment. Otherwise one invites only danger and humiliation.

sentences.zh: 故鼎之為國，專以固本為先，根本固而後敵可圖、讎可復，此鼎之心也。

translations.literal: Therefore in serving the state Ding put consolidating the foundation first—once the root is firm, then the enemy can be plotted against and the foe recovered; this was Ding's heart.
translations.idiomatic: Ding's policy for the state put consolidation first. Only when the foundation was firm could the enemy be overcome and the wrong avenged. That was Ding's conviction.

sentences.zh: 惜乎一見忌于秦檜，斥逐遠徙，卒齎其志而亡，君子所尤痛心也。

translations.literal: Alas—once he met with Qin Hui's envy, he was driven out and exiled far; in the end he brought his ambition with him to death—the thing that gentlemen lament most bitterly.
translations.idiomatic: Alas, once Qin Hui turned against him, Ding was driven out and exiled to distant regions, and in the end he died with his ambition unfulfilled—a loss that men of honor mourn above all.

sentences.zh: 竊嘗論澤、鼎之終而益有感焉。

translations.literal: I have privately reflected on the ends of Ze and Ding and been all the more moved.
translations.idiomatic: Reflecting on the ends of Zong Ze and Zhao Ding, I am moved all the more.

sentences.zh: 澤之易簀也，猶連呼「渡河」者三；

translations.literal: At Ze's changing of the mat, he still thrice cried out "Cross the river";
translations.idiomatic: On his deathbed Ze still cried "Cross the river!" three times;

sentences.zh: 而鼎自題其銘旌，有「氣作山河壯本朝」之語。

translations.literal: while Ding himself inscribed his funeral banner with the words "His spirit makes the rivers and mountains mighty for our dynasty."
translations.idiomatic: and Ding himself wrote on his funeral banner, "His spirit makes the rivers and mountains mighty for our dynasty."

sentences.zh: 何二臣之愛君憂國，雖處死生禍變之際，而猶不渝若是！

translations.literal: How these two ministers loved their sovereign and grieved for the state—even amid the turn of life and death and calamity and change they still did not waver thus!
translations.idiomatic: What love of sovereign and care for the state these two ministers showed—even at the brink of death and amid ruin, they did not waver!

sentences.zh: 而高宗惑於憸邪之口，乍任乍黜，所謂「善善而不能用」，千載而下，忠臣義士猶為之撫卷扼腕，國之不競，有以哉！

translations.literal: Yet Gaozong was deluded by slanderous and wicked mouths, appointing and dismissing by turns—the so-called "good at recognizing goodness yet unable to employ it"; a thousand years hence loyal ministers and righteous men still press the scroll and wring their wrists at it—the state's failure to prevail has its cause!
translations.idiomatic: Yet Gaozong was misled by slanderous men, appointing good officials only to dismiss them again—the very case of "recognizing virtue yet failing to use it." A thousand years on, loyal ministers and righteous men still close the scroll and wring their hands. That the state failed to prevail has its cause indeed!
